`capture/src/maps.rs`:

```rs
//! What a map wrote. While a capture records, a map hands the game memory locum owns (a shadow), copied whole to the
//! driver's at the unmap, and only the bytes the game wrote are recorded: those that differ from what the shadow
//! started as. A discarding map's shadow starts as [`fill`]'s pattern, so the GPU sees that pattern wherever the game
//! wrote nothing, and a replay of the map writes the same pattern before the bytes recorded.

/// The pattern's 4-byte word at word `i`.
fn pattern(i: usize) -> u32 {
    (i as u32).wrapping_mul(0x9e37_79b9) ^ 0x5bd1_e995
}

/// Fills `data` with the pattern a discarding map starts as.
pub fn fill(data: &mut [u8]) {
    for (i, chunk) in data.chunks_mut(4).enumerate() {
        let p = pattern(i).to_le_bytes();
        chunk.copy_from_slice(&p[..chunk.len()]);
    }
}

/// The byte ranges (start, end) of `data` that differ from `reference` (or from the pattern), merged across gaps of
/// 64 bytes: what a map records.
pub fn written(data: &[u8], reference: Option<&[u8]>) -> Vec<(usize, usize)> {
    differing(data, reference, 64)
}

/// The byte ranges of `data` that differ from `reference` (or from the pattern), word by word with nothing between
/// them: what an unmap copies back, so it writes no byte the game did not write.
pub fn changed(data: &[u8], reference: Option<&[u8]>) -> Vec<(usize, usize)> {
    differing(data, reference, 0)
}

fn differing(data: &[u8], reference: Option<&[u8]>, gap: usize) -> Vec<(usize, usize)> {
    let mut ranges: Vec<(usize, usize)> = Vec::new();
    for (i, chunk) in data.chunks(4).enumerate() {
        let differs = match reference {
            Some(r) => chunk != &r[i * 4..i * 4 + chunk.len()],
            None => chunk != &pattern(i).to_le_bytes()[..chunk.len()],
        };
        if !differs {
            continue;
        }
        let (start, end) = (i * 4, i * 4 + chunk.len());
        match ranges.last_mut() {
            Some(last) if start <= last.1 + gap => last.1 = end,
            _ => ranges.push((start, end)),
        }
    }
    ranges
}

/// The bytes a discarding map of `size` bytes left, given the ranges it wrote (offset, length) and their bytes one
/// after another.
pub fn discarded(size: usize, ranges: &[(usize, usize)], bytes: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut out = vec![0u8; size];
    fill(&mut out);
    let mut at = 0;
    for &(offset, len) in ranges {
        if let (Some(dst), Some(src)) = (out.get_mut(offset..offset + len), bytes.get(at..at + len)) {
            dst.copy_from_slice(src);
        }
        at += len;
    }
    out
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn a_discarding_map_replays_to_the_bytes_the_gpu_saw() {
        let mut shadow = vec![0u8; 1000];
        fill(&mut shadow);
        shadow[8..88].fill(7);
        shadow[600..604].copy_from_slice(&1.5f32.to_le_bytes());
        let ranges = written(&shadow, None);
        assert_eq!(ranges, vec![(8, 88), (600, 604)]);
        // An unmap copies back only the words written.
        let mut reference = shadow.clone();
        reference[40..44].copy_from_slice(&[9, 9, 9, 9]);
        reference[52..56].copy_from_slice(&[9, 9, 9, 9]);
        assert_eq!(changed(&shadow, Some(&reference)), vec![(40, 44), (52, 56)]);
        assert_eq!(written(&shadow, Some(&reference)), vec![(40, 56)]);
        let bytes: Vec<u8> = ranges.iter().flat_map(|&(a, b)| shadow[a..b].to_vec()).collect();
        let spans: Vec<(usize, usize)> = ranges.iter().map(|&(a, b)| (a, b - a)).collect();
        assert_eq!(discarded(1000, &spans, &bytes), shadow);
        // Nothing written: the GPU saw the pattern alone.
        let mut empty = vec![0u8; 64];
        fill(&mut empty);
        assert!(written(&empty, None).is_empty());
        assert_eq!(discarded(64, &[], &[]), empty);
    }
}
```

`capture/src/rdef.rs`:

```rs
//! Shader reflection from a DXBC container's `RDEF` chunk: each constant buffer's name, register and variables, so a
//! constant can be shown as `cbTexScroll.uvScale.x` instead of `b11 c0.x`.

/// A DXBC container's chunk with the four-character code `code`.
pub fn chunk<'a>(dxbc: &'a [u8], code: &[u8; 4]) -> Option<&'a [u8]> {
    if dxbc.get(..4)? != b"DXBC" {
        return None;
    }
    let count = u32_at(dxbc, 28)? as usize;
    for i in 0..count {
        let offset = u32_at(dxbc, 32 + i * 4)? as usize;
        if dxbc.get(offset..offset + 4)? == code {
            let size = u32_at(dxbc, offset + 4)? as usize;
            return dxbc.get(offset + 8..offset + 8 + size);
        }
    }
    None
}

fn u32_at(b: &[u8], at: usize) -> Option<u32> {
    Some(u32::from_le_bytes(b.get(at..at + 4)?.try_into().ok()?))
}

fn u16_at(b: &[u8], at: usize) -> Option<u16> {
    Some(u16::from_le_bytes(b.get(at..at + 2)?.try_into().ok()?))
}

fn str_at(b: &[u8], at: usize) -> Option<String> {
    let rest = b.get(at..)?;
    let end = rest.iter().position(|&c| c == 0)?;
    Some(String::from_utf8_lossy(&rest[..end]).into_owned())
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct Type {
    /// D3D_SHADER_VARIABLE_CLASS: 0 scalar, 1 vector, 2 row-major matrix, 3 column-major matrix, 4 object, 5 struct.
    pub class: u16,
    /// D3D_SHADER_VARIABLE_TYPE: 1 bool, 2 int, 3 float, 19 uint, ...
    pub base: u16,
    pub rows: u16,
    pub columns: u16,
    /// Array length, 0 when not an array.
    pub elements: u16,
    pub members: Vec<Member>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct Member {
    pub name: String,
    pub offset: u32,
    pub ty: Type,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct Variable {
    pub name: String,
    pub offset: u32,
    pub size: u32,
    /// Whether the shader reads it.
    pub used: bool,
    pub ty: Type,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct ConstantBuffer {
    pub name: String,
    /// The register (`b<slot>`), when the shader binds it.
    pub slot: Option<u32>,
    pub space: u32,
    pub size: u32,
    pub variables: Vec<Variable>,
}

impl Type {
    /// HLSL spelling, like `float4`, `float4x4` or `uint`.
    pub fn name(&self) -> String {
        let base = match self.base {
            0 => "void",
            1 => "bool",
            2 => "int",
            3 => "float",
            19 => "uint",
            20 => "uint8",
            39 => "double",
            54 => "min8float",
            55 => "min10float",
            56 => "min16float",
            57 => "min12int",
            58 => "min16int",
            59 => "min16uint",
            _ => "?",
        };
        let shape = match self.class {
            0 => base.to_string(),
            1 => format!("{base}{}", self.columns),
            2 | 3 => format!("{base}{}x{}", self.rows, self.columns),
            5 => "struct".to_string(),
            _ => base.to_string(),
        };
        if self.elements > 0 {
            format!("{shape}[{}]", self.elements)
        } else {
            shape
        }
    }
}

fn read_type(rdef: &[u8], at: usize, depth: u32) -> Option<Type> {
    let mut t = Type {
        class: u16_at(rdef, at)?,
        base: u16_at(rdef, at + 2)?,
        rows: u16_at(rdef, at + 4)?,
        columns: u16_at(rdef, at + 6)?,
        elements: u16_at(rdef, at + 8)?,
        members: Vec::new(),
    };
    let members = u16_at(rdef, at + 10)? as usize;
    let members_at = u32_at(rdef, at + 12)? as usize;
    if depth < 8 {
        for i in 0..members {
            let m = members_at + i * 12;
            let name = str_at(rdef, u32_at(rdef, m)? as usize)?;
            let ty = read_type(rdef, u32_at(rdef, m + 4)? as usize, depth + 1)?;
            t.members.push(Member {
                name,
                offset: u32_at(rdef, m + 8)?,
                ty,
            });
        }
    }
    Some(t)
}

/// The constant buffers a shader declares, from its DXBC bytecode.
pub fn constant_buffers(dxbc: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<ConstantBuffer>> {
    let rdef = chunk(dxbc, b"RDEF")?;
    let cb_count = u32_at(rdef, 0)? as usize;
    let cb_at = u32_at(rdef, 4)? as usize;
    let bind_count = u32_at(rdef, 8)? as usize;
    let bind_at = u32_at(rdef, 12)? as usize;
    let major = rdef.get(17).copied()?;
    // Shader model 5 adds an "RD11" header after the creator's name offset: its own size, then the sizes of a
    // constant buffer, a binding, a variable, a type and a member record (24, 32 or 40 with 5.1's register space,
    // 40, 36, 12). Before it, variables are 24 bytes and bindings 32.
    let rd11 = major >= 5 && rdef.get(28..32) == Some(b"RD11");
    let (cb_size, bind_size, var_size) = if rd11 {
        (
            u32_at(rdef, 36)? as usize,
            u32_at(rdef, 40)? as usize,
            u32_at(rdef, 44)? as usize,
        )
    } else {
        (24, 32, 24)
    };
    // Constant buffers are bound by name: the binding of type 0 (cbuffer) with the same name gives the register.
    let mut registers = Vec::new();
    for i in 0..bind_count {
        let b = bind_at + i * bind_size;
        let name = str_at(rdef, u32_at(rdef, b)? as usize)?;
        let kind = u32_at(rdef, b + 4)?;
        let slot = u32_at(rdef, b + 20)?;
        let space = if bind_size >= 40 { u32_at(rdef, b + 32)? } else { 0 };
        if kind == 0 {
            registers.push((name, slot, space));
        }
    }
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(cb_count);
    for i in 0..cb_count {
        let c = cb_at + i * cb_size;
        let name = str_at(rdef, u32_at(rdef, c)? as usize)?;
        let var_count = u32_at(rdef, c + 4)? as usize;
        let var_at = u32_at(rdef, c + 8)? as usize;
        let size = u32_at(rdef, c + 12)?;
        let mut variables = Vec::with_capacity(var_count);
        for v in 0..var_count {
            let at = var_at + v * var_size;
            variables.push(Variable {
                name: str_at(rdef, u32_at(rdef, at)? as usize)?,
                offset: u32_at(rdef, at + 4)?,
                size: u32_at(rdef, at + 8)?,
                used: u32_at(rdef, at + 12)? & 2 != 0,
                ty: read_type(rdef, u32_at(rdef, at + 16)? as usize, 0)?,
            });
        }
        let (slot, space) = registers
            .iter()
            .find(|(n, _, _)| *n == name)
            .map_or((None, 0), |&(_, s, sp)| (Some(s), sp));
        out.push(ConstantBuffer {
            name,
            slot,
            space,
            size,
            variables,
        });
    }
    Some(out)
}

const COMPONENTS: [&str; 4] = ["x", "y", "z", "w"];

/// The name of the 4-byte value at `offset` in a variable of type `ty` called `name`, like `uvScale.y`,
/// `bones[3][1].z` or `light.color.x`, and its base type. HLSL packs arrays and structs in 16-byte registers.
fn name_in(name: &str, ty: &Type, offset: u32) -> (String, u16) {
    if ty.elements > 0 {
        let element = Type {
            elements: 0,
            ..ty.clone()
        };
        let stride = element_stride(&element);
        let i = (offset / stride).min(u32::from(ty.elements) - 1);
        return name_in(&format!("{name}[{i}]"), &element, offset - i * stride);
    }
    match ty.class {
        5 => {
            let member = ty.members.iter().rev().find(|m| m.offset <= offset);
            match member {
                Some(m) => name_in(&format!("{name}.{}", m.name), &m.ty, offset - m.offset),
                None => (name.to_string(), ty.base),
            }
        }
        2 | 3 => {
            // Row-major: each row is a register; column-major: each column is.
            let (major, minor) = (offset / 16, (offset % 16) / 4);
            let (r, c) = if ty.class == 2 {
                (major, minor)
            } else {
                (minor, major)
            };
            (format!("{name}[{r}][{c}]"), ty.base)
        }
        1 => (
            format!("{name}.{}", COMPONENTS[((offset / 4) % 4) as usize]),
            ty.base,
        ),
        _ => (name.to_string(), ty.base),
    }
}

/// The bytes one array element of `ty` takes in a constant buffer (every element but the last starts a register).
fn element_stride(ty: &Type) -> u32 {
    let bytes = match ty.class {
        5 => ty
            .members
            .iter()
            .map(|m| m.offset + element_stride(&m.ty) * u32::from(m.ty.elements.max(1)))
            .max()
            .unwrap_or(16),
        2 => u32::from(ty.rows) * 16,
        3 => u32::from(ty.columns) * 16,
        _ => u32::from(ty.columns.max(1)) * 4,
    };
    bytes.div_ceil(16) * 16
}

impl ConstantBuffer {
    /// The name of the 4-byte value at `offset` bytes into the buffer, if a variable covers it.
    pub fn name_at(&self, offset: u32) -> Option<String> {
        self.at(offset).map(|(name, _)| name)
    }

    /// The name of the 4-byte value at `offset` bytes into the buffer and its base type (`D3D_SHADER_VARIABLE_TYPE`:
    /// 1 bool, 2 int, 3 float, 19 uint), if a variable covers it.
    pub fn at(&self, offset: u32) -> Option<(String, u16)> {
        let v = self
            .variables
            .iter()
            .find(|v| (v.offset..v.offset + v.size).contains(&offset))?;
        Some(name_in(
            &format!("{}.{}", self.name, v.name),
            &v.ty,
            offset - v.offset,
        ))
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {

    }

    #[test]
    fn variables_after_the_first_use_the_variable_record_size() {

        let mut r = vec![0u8; 400];

        let text = |r: &mut Vec<u8>, at: usize, t: &str| r[at..at + t.len()].copy_from_slice(t.as_bytes());
        // cb count, cb at, binding count, binding at, version 5.0 pixel, flags, creator.
```

`capture/src/rules.rs`:

```rs
//! The rules that change what is drawn, shared by locum in the game (`overrides.txt`) and by replay. One rule per
//! line, `#` starts a comment:
//!
//! - `skip vs=<hash>`: draws with that shader bound are not drawn (`skip cs=<hash>`: dispatches are not run);
//! - `solid vs=<hash> R G B A`: draws with that shader bound get a pixel shader writing that colour to every target;
//! - `shader ps=<hash> FILE`: that shader is replaced by the bytecode in FILE (relative to the rules' folder);
//! - `constant ps b3 c0 X Y Z W`: the draw sees constant 0 of its ps b3 buffer (counted from the first constant
//!   bound) as X Y Z W; a value is a float or `0x` and 8 hex digits (raw bits).
//!
//! Any rule can end with conditions, `if vs=<hash> ps=<hash>`, all of which must hold; `vs=<hash>` after `skip`,
//! `solid` and `shader` is such a condition too. Any stage can be named: vs hs ds gs ps cs. Stages are numbered in
//! that order (as in the capture's `draws` table). In the game a hash is the whole hash; replay also takes the start of
//! one, if it names exactly one shader of that stage in the capture.

use std::path::Path;

/// The stages by number.
pub const STAGES: [&str; 6] = ["vs", "hs", "ds", "gs", "ps", "cs"];
pub const PIXEL: usize = 4;
pub const COMPUTE: usize = 5;
/// Constant-buffer slots a stage has, and constants (16 bytes) a buffer can hold.
pub const CB_SLOTS: u32 = 14;
pub const CONSTANTS: u32 = 4096;

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum Action {
    Skip,
    /// A pixel shader writing one colour.
    Solid([f32; 4]),
    /// A shader of the rule's stage, from bytecode.
    Shader(Vec<u8>),
    Constant {
        slot: u32,
        index: u32,
        bits: [u32; 4],
    },
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Rule {
    pub text: String,
    /// The stage the rule changes (pixel for `solid`).
    pub stage: usize,
    /// Shaders that must be bound, by stage.
    pub when: Vec<(usize, u64)>,
    pub action: Action,
}

pub fn stage_named(name: &str) -> Option<usize> {
    STAGES.iter().position(|s| *s == name)
}

/// How the hash in `stage=hash` names a shader, given the stage's number and the text after `=`.
pub type Resolve<'a> = &'a dyn Fn(usize, &str) -> Result<u64, String>;

/// The text read as the hash, in hex: for the game, where a rule can name a shader made after it is read.
pub fn hex(_stage: usize, hash: &str) -> Result<u64, String> {
    u64::from_str_radix(hash, 16).map_err(|_| format!("{hash:?} is not a hex hash"))
}

/// `vs=0123456789abcdef`.
fn condition(word: &str, resolve: Resolve) -> Result<(usize, u64), String> {
    let (stage, hash) = word
        .split_once('=')
        .ok_or_else(|| format!("{word:?} is not stage=hash"))?;
    let stage = stage_named(stage).ok_or_else(|| format!("unknown stage {stage:?}"))?;
    Ok((stage, resolve(stage, hash)?))
}

fn value_bits(word: &str) -> Result<u32, String> {
    if let Some(hex) = word.strip_prefix("0x") {
        return u32::from_str_radix(hex, 16).map_err(|_| format!("{word:?} is not 0x and hex digits"));
    }
    word.parse::<f32>()
        .map(f32::to_bits)
        .map_err(|_| format!("{word:?} is not a number"))
}

fn numbered(word: Option<&str>, prefix: char, what: &str) -> Result<u32, String> {
    word.and_then(|w| w.strip_prefix(prefix))
        .and_then(|n| n.parse().ok())
        .ok_or_else(|| format!("expected {what} ({prefix}N)"))
}

/// One rule; `dir` is where a `shader` rule's file is looked for, and `resolve` names the shaders.
pub fn parse(line: &str, dir: &Path, resolve: Resolve) -> Result<Rule, String> {
    let (body, conditions) = match line.split_once(" if ") {
        Some((b, c)) => (
            b,
            c.split_whitespace()
                .map(|w| condition(w, resolve))
                .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?,
        ),
        None => (line, Vec::new()),
    };
    let mut words = body.split_whitespace();
    let verb = words.next().ok_or("empty rule")?;
    let mut when = conditions;
    let (stage, action) = match verb {
        "skip" | "solid" | "shader" => {
            let first = condition(words.next().ok_or("expected stage=hash")?, resolve)?;
            when.insert(0, first);
            match verb {
                "skip" => (first.0, Action::Skip),
                "solid" => {
                    let mut c = [0f32; 4];
                    for v in &mut c {
                        let w = words.next().ok_or("solid needs R G B A")?;
                        *v = w.parse().map_err(|_| format!("{w:?} is not a number"))?;
                    }
                    (PIXEL, Action::Solid(c))
                }
                _ => {
                    let file = words.next().ok_or("shader needs a file")?;
                    let code = std::fs::read(dir.join(file)).map_err(|e| format!("{file}: {e}"))?;
                    (first.0, Action::Shader(code))
                }
            }
        }
        "constant" => {
            let stage = words
                .next()
                .and_then(stage_named)
                .ok_or("constant needs a stage")?;
            let slot = numbered(words.next(), 'b', "a constant buffer slot")?;
            let index = numbered(words.next(), 'c', "a constant")?;
            let mut bits = [0u32; 4];
            for b in &mut bits {
                *b = value_bits(words.next().ok_or("constant needs X Y Z W")?)?;
            }
            if slot >= CB_SLOTS || index >= CONSTANTS {
                return Err("slot or constant out of range".into());
            }
            (stage, Action::Constant { slot, index, bits })
        }
        other => return Err(format!("unknown rule {other:?}")),
    };
    if let Some(extra) = words.next() {
        return Err(format!("unexpected {extra:?}"));
    }
    Ok(Rule {
        text: line.to_string(),
        stage,
        when,
        action,
    })
}

/// Every rule in `text`, and for each line that is not one, its number (from 1) and why.
pub fn parse_all(text: &str, dir: &Path, resolve: Resolve) -> (Vec<Rule>, Vec<(usize, String)>) {
    let (mut rules, mut errors) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
    for (n, line) in text.lines().enumerate() {
        let line = line.split('#').next().unwrap_or("").trim();
        if line.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        match parse(line, dir, resolve) {
            Ok(r) => rules.push(r),
            Err(e) => errors.push((n + 1, e)),
        }
    }
    (rules, errors)
}

impl Rule {
    /// Whether the rule is for a dispatch (`compute`) or a draw.
    pub fn applies(&self, compute: bool) -> bool {
        compute == (self.stage == COMPUTE)
    }

    /// Whether its conditions hold, given the hash of the shader bound at each stage.
    pub fn holds(&self, mut hash: impl FnMut(usize) -> Option<u64>) -> bool {
        self.when.iter().all(|&(stage, h)| hash(stage) == Some(h))
    }
}

/// HLSL (shader model 5) for a pixel shader writing `colour` to all eight targets.
pub fn solid_source(colour: &[f32; 4]) -> String {
    let [r, g, b, a] = colour;
    let targets: String = (0..8).map(|i| format!("float4 c{i} : SV_Target{i}; ")).collect();
    let fill: String = (0..8).map(|i| format!("o.c{i} = k; ")).collect();
    format!(
        "struct O {{ {targets}}}; O main() {{ float4 k = float4({r:?}, {g:?}, {b:?}, {a:?}); O o; {fill}return o; }}"
    )
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::path::PathBuf;

    fn rule(line: &str) -> Result<Rule, String> {
        parse(line, &PathBuf::from("."), &hex)
    }

    #[test]
    fn rules_parse() {
        let r = rule("skip vs=00000000000000ff if ps=10").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(r.action, Action::Skip);
        assert_eq!(r.when, vec![(0, 0xff), (4, 0x10)]);
        let r = rule("constant vs b11 c0 4 4 0x3f800000 -1.5").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            r.action,
            Action::Constant {
                slot: 11,
                index: 0,
                bits: [
                    4f32.to_bits(),
                    4f32.to_bits(),
                    1f32.to_bits(),
                    (-1.5f32).to_bits()
                ]
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(
            rule("solid vs=1 1 0 1 1").unwrap().action,
            Action::Solid([1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0])
        );
        assert!(rule("constant vs b14 c0 0 0 0 0").is_err());
        assert!(rule("skip vs").is_err());
        assert!(rule("frobnicate").is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn conditions() {
        let r = rule("skip cs=ab if vs=1").unwrap();
        assert!(r.applies(true) && !r.applies(false));
        assert!(r.holds(|s| Some(if s == COMPUTE { 0xab } else { 1 })));
        assert!(!r.holds(|_| None));
    }
}
```

`capture/src/stacks.rs`:

```rs
//! Call stacks and the process's modules, for tying a call back to the code that made it.

use core::ffi::c_void;
use std::sync::OnceLock;

use windows::Win32::Foundation::HMODULE;
use windows::Win32::System::Diagnostics::Debug::RtlCaptureStackBackTrace;
use windows::Win32::System::LibraryLoader::{
    GET_MODULE_HANDLE_EX_FLAG_FROM_ADDRESS, GET_MODULE_HANDLE_EX_FLAG_UNCHANGED_REFCOUNT, GetModuleHandleExW,
};
use windows::Win32::System::ProcessStatus::{
    EnumProcessModules, GetModuleFileNameExW, GetModuleInformation, MODULEINFO,
};
use windows::Win32::System::Threading::GetCurrentProcess;
use windows::core::PCWSTR;

use crate::db::Module;

/// The address range of the module this code is in (locum's own), whose frames stacks leave out.
fn own_range() -> (u64, u64) {
    static RANGE: OnceLock<(u64, u64)> = OnceLock::new();
    *RANGE.get_or_init(|| {
        let mut module = HMODULE::default();
        let flags = GET_MODULE_HANDLE_EX_FLAG_FROM_ADDRESS | GET_MODULE_HANDLE_EX_FLAG_UNCHANGED_REFCOUNT;
        let here = own_range as *const c_void;
        if unsafe { GetModuleHandleExW(flags, PCWSTR(here.cast()), &mut module) }.is_err() {
            return (0, 0);
        }
        let mut info = MODULEINFO::default();
        let ok = unsafe {
            GetModuleInformation(
                GetCurrentProcess(),
                module,
                &mut info,
                size_of::<MODULEINFO>() as u32,
            )
        };
        if ok.is_err() {
            return (0, 0);
        }
        let base = info.lpBaseOfDll as u64;
        (base, base + u64::from(info.SizeOfImage))
    })
}

/// The return addresses of the calling thread's stack, innermost first, without locum's own frames: the first
/// address is in the code that called into locum.
pub fn capture() -> Vec<u64> {
    let mut frames = [core::ptr::null_mut::<c_void>(); 48];
    let n = unsafe { RtlCaptureStackBackTrace(1, &mut frames, None) } as usize;
    let (lo, hi) = own_range();
    frames[..n]
        .iter()
        .map(|&f| f as u64)
        .filter(|&f| !(lo..hi).contains(&f))
        .collect()
}

/// Every module loaded in the process.
pub fn modules() -> Vec<Module> {
    let process = unsafe { GetCurrentProcess() };
    let mut handles = vec![HMODULE::default(); 1024];
    let mut needed = 0u32;
    loop {
        let bytes = (handles.len() * size_of::<HMODULE>()) as u32;
        if unsafe { EnumProcessModules(process, handles.as_mut_ptr(), bytes, &mut needed) }.is_err() {
            return Vec::new();
        }
        let count = needed as usize / size_of::<HMODULE>();
        if count <= handles.len() {
            handles.truncate(count);
            break;
        }
        handles.resize(count, HMODULE::default());
    }
    handles
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .filter_map(|(i, &m)| {
            let mut info = MODULEINFO::default();
            unsafe { GetModuleInformation(process, m, &mut info, size_of::<MODULEINFO>() as u32) }.ok()?;
            let mut name = [0u16; 1024];
            let len = unsafe { GetModuleFileNameExW(Some(process), Some(m), &mut name) } as usize;
            Some(Module {
                id: i as u64,
                path: String::from_utf16_lossy(&name[..len]),
                base: info.lpBaseOfDll as u64,
                size: u64::from(info.SizeOfImage),
            })
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Gives each distinct stack a number, for the `stacks` table.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Interner {
    ids: std::collections::HashMap<Vec<u64>, u64>,
}

impl Interner {
    pub fn id(&mut self, frames: &[u64]) -> Option<u64> {
        if frames.is_empty() {
            return None;
        }
        let next = self.ids.len() as u64 + 1;
        Some(*self.ids.entry(frames.to_vec()).or_insert(next))
    }

    pub fn into_rows(self) -> Vec<(u64, Vec<u64>)> {
        let mut rows: Vec<(u64, Vec<u64>)> = self.ids.into_iter().map(|(f, id)| (id, f)).collect();
        rows.sort_by_key(|r| r.0);
        rows
    }
}
```

`capture/src/texels.rs`:

```rs
//! Reading texels: one subresource of a DXGI format, in the canonical layout, as RGBA floats, and those as 8-bit
//! pixels for a picture. Block-compressed formats are decoded to 8 bits a channel first (BC6H too, so its values are
//! clamped to 0..1); BC4 and BC5 are read as unsigned.

use crate::format;

/// An image of RGBA floats; `channels` says how many of them the format has (1 for depth and single-channel formats).
pub struct Image {
    pub width: u32,
    pub height: u32,
    pub channels: u8,
    /// Whether the values are unbounded (float formats), not 0..1 or integers.
    pub float: bool,
    pub texels: Vec<[f32; 4]>,
}

/// How values are mapped to 0..255 for a picture.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum Range {
    /// Single-channel images stretched from their smallest to their largest finite value; float colour tone-mapped;
    /// the rest clamped.
    Auto,
    Clamp,
    /// x / (1 + x) per channel.
    Tonemap,
    /// From the first value to the second.
    Fixed(f32, f32),
}

impl Range {
    /// `auto`, `clamp`, `tonemap` or `LO:HI`.
    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Option<Range> {
        match s {
            "auto" => Some(Range::Auto),
            "clamp" => Some(Range::Clamp),
            "tonemap" => Some(Range::Tonemap),
            _ => {
                let (lo, hi) = s.split_once(':')?;
                Some(Range::Fixed(lo.trim().parse().ok()?, hi.trim().parse().ok()?))
            }
        }
    }
}

/// A half-precision float's value.
pub fn f16(bits: u16) -> f32 {
    let sign = if bits & 0x8000 != 0 { -1.0 } else { 1.0 };
    let exp = i32::from((bits >> 10) & 31);
    let mant = f32::from(bits & 0x3ff);
    sign * match exp {
        0 => mant * 2f32.powi(-24),
        31 if mant == 0.0 => f32::INFINITY,
        31 => f32::NAN,
        e => (1.0 + mant / 1024.0) * 2f32.powi(e - 15),
    }
}

/// An unsigned float with a 5-bit exponent and `mantissa` bits (R11G11B10_FLOAT).
fn small_float(bits: u32, mantissa: u32) -> f32 {
    let exp = ((bits >> mantissa) & 31) as i32;
    let mant = (bits & ((1 << mantissa) - 1)) as f32 / (1 << mantissa) as f32;
    match exp {
        0 => mant * 2f32.powi(-14),
        31 => f32::INFINITY,
        e => (1.0 + mant) * 2f32.powi(e - 15),
    }
}

/// How a plain format's texel is read: `n` channels of `bits` each, as `kind`.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
enum Kind {
    Float,
    Unorm,
    Snorm,
    Uint,
    Sint,
}

fn plain(format: u32) -> Option<(u8, u32, Kind)> {
    use Kind::*;
    Some(match format {
        2 => (4, 32, Float),
        3 => (4, 32, Uint),
        4 => (4, 32, Sint),
        6 => (3, 32, Float),
        7 => (3, 32, Uint),
        8 => (3, 32, Sint),
        10 => (4, 16, Float),
        11 => (4, 16, Unorm),
        12 => (4, 16, Uint),
        13 => (4, 16, Snorm),
        14 => (4, 16, Sint),
        16 => (2, 32, Float),
        17 => (2, 32, Uint),
        18 => (2, 32, Sint),
        28 | 29 => (4, 8, Unorm),
        30 => (4, 8, Uint),
        31 => (4, 8, Snorm),
        32 => (4, 8, Sint),
        34 => (2, 16, Float),
        35 => (2, 16, Unorm),
        36 => (2, 16, Uint),
        37 => (2, 16, Snorm),
        38 => (2, 16, Sint),
        41 => (1, 32, Float),
        42 => (1, 32, Uint),
        43 => (1, 32, Sint),
        49 => (2, 8, Unorm),
        50 => (2, 8, Uint),
        51 => (2, 8, Snorm),
        52 => (2, 8, Sint),
        54 => (1, 16, Float),
        56 => (1, 16, Unorm),
        57 => (1, 16, Uint),
        58 => (1, 16, Snorm),
        59 => (1, 16, Sint),
        61 => (1, 8, Unorm),
        62 => (1, 8, Uint),
        63 => (1, 8, Snorm),
        64 => (1, 8, Sint),
        _ => return None,
    })
}

fn channel(bytes: &[u8], bits: u32, kind: Kind) -> f32 {
    match (bits, kind) {
        (32, Kind::Float) => f32::from_le_bytes(bytes[..4].try_into().unwrap()),
        (32, Kind::Uint) => u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[..4].try_into().unwrap()) as f32,
        (32, _) => i32::from_le_bytes(bytes[..4].try_into().unwrap()) as f32,
        (16, k) => {
            let v = u16::from_le_bytes(bytes[..2].try_into().unwrap());
            match k {
                Kind::Float => f16(v),
                Kind::Unorm => f32::from(v) / 65535.0,
                Kind::Snorm => (f32::from(v as i16) / 32767.0).max(-1.0),
                Kind::Uint => f32::from(v),
                Kind::Sint => f32::from(v as i16),
            }
        }
        (_, k) => {
            let v = bytes[0];
            match k {
                Kind::Unorm | Kind::Float => f32::from(v) / 255.0,
                Kind::Snorm => (f32::from(v as i8) / 127.0).max(-1.0),
                Kind::Uint => f32::from(v),
                Kind::Sint => f32::from(v as i8),
            }
        }
    }
}

type BlockFn = fn(&[u8], &mut [u32]);

fn block_decoder(format: u32) -> Option<(BlockFn, u8)> {
    use texture2ddecoder as t;
    Some(match format {
        71 | 72 => (t::decode_bc1_block as BlockFn, 4),
        74 | 75 => (t::decode_bc2_block, 4),
        77 | 78 => (t::decode_bc3_block, 4),
        80 | 81 => (t::decode_bc4_block, 1),
        83 | 84 => (t::decode_bc5_block, 2),
        95 => (t::decode_bc6_block_unsigned, 3),
        96 => (t::decode_bc6_block_signed, 3),
        98 | 99 => (t::decode_bc7_block, 4),
        _ => return None,
    })
}

/// Decodes one subresource of `width` x `height` texels (one depth slice of a volume: pass its bytes only).
pub fn decode(format: u32, width: u32, height: u32, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Image, String> {
    let format = format::readable(format);
    let layout = format::layout(format).ok_or_else(|| format!("{} has no layout", format::name(format)))?;
    let need = u64::from(layout.row_bytes(width)) * u64::from(layout.rows(height));
    if (bytes.len() as u64) < need {
        return Err(format!("{} bytes, {need} needed", bytes.len()));
    }
    let (w, h) = (width as usize, height as usize);
    let mut texels = vec![[0f32; 4]; w * h];
    let mut float = false;
    let channels;
    if let Some((decode_block, n)) = block_decoder(format) {
        channels = n;
        let row_bytes = layout.row_bytes(width) as usize;
        let block_bytes = layout.block_bytes as usize;
        let mut out = [0u32; 16];
        for by in 0..h.div_ceil(4) {
            for bx in 0..w.div_ceil(4) {
                let at = by * row_bytes + bx * block_bytes;
                out.fill(0);
                decode_block(&bytes[at..at + block_bytes], &mut out);
                for (i, px) in out.iter().enumerate() {
                    let (x, y) = (bx * 4 + i % 4, by * 4 + i / 4);
                    if x < w && y < h {
                        let [b, g, r, a] = px.to_le_bytes();
                        texels[y * w + x] = [r, g, b, a].map(|c| f32::from(c) / 255.0);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        if n < 4 {
            for t in &mut texels {
                t[3] = 1.0;
            }
        }
    } else if let Some((n, bits, kind)) = plain(format) {
        channels = n;
        float = matches!(kind, Kind::Float);
        let size = (bits / 8) as usize;
        for (i, t) in texels.iter_mut().enumerate() {
            let at = i * size * n as usize;
            for c in 0..n as usize {
                t[c] = channel(&bytes[at + c * size..], bits, kind);
            }
            if n < 4 {
                t[3] = 1.0;
            }
        }
    } else {
        let word = |i: usize| u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[i * 4..i * 4 + 4].try_into().unwrap());
        let half = |i: usize| u16::from_le_bytes(bytes[i * 2..i * 2 + 2].try_into().unwrap());
        match format {
            // R10G10B10A2_UNORM / UINT
            24 | 25 => {
                channels = 4;
                let scale = if format == 24 {
                    [1023.0, 1023.0, 1023.0, 3.0]
                } else {
                    [1.0; 4]
                };
                for (i, t) in texels.iter_mut().enumerate() {
                    let v = word(i);
                    let c = [v & 1023, (v >> 10) & 1023, (v >> 20) & 1023, v >> 30];
                    *t = [0, 1, 2, 3].map(|k| c[k] as f32 / scale[k]);
                }
            }
            26 => {
                channels = 3;
                float = true;
                for (i, t) in texels.iter_mut().enumerate() {
                    let v = word(i);
                    *t = [
                        small_float(v & 0x7ff, 6),
                        small_float((v >> 11) & 0x7ff, 6),
                        small_float(v >> 22, 5),
                        1.0,
                    ];
                }
            }
            // R32_FLOAT_X8X24: the depth of D32_FLOAT_S8X24; the stencil word is left out.
            21 => {
                channels = 1;
                float = true;
                for (i, t) in texels.iter_mut().enumerate() {
                    *t = [f32::from_bits(word(i * 2)), 0.0, 0.0, 1.0];
                }
            }
            // R24_UNORM_X8: the depth of D24_UNORM_S8.
            46 => {
                channels = 1;
                for (i, t) in texels.iter_mut().enumerate() {
                    *t = [(word(i) & 0xff_ffff) as f32 / 16_777_215.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0];
                }
            }
            65 => {
                channels = 4;
                for (i, t) in texels.iter_mut().enumerate() {
                    *t = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, f32::from(bytes[i]) / 255.0];
                }
            }
            67 => {
                channels = 3;
                float = true;
                for (i, t) in texels.iter_mut().enumerate() {
                    let v = word(i);
                    let scale = 2f32.powi((v >> 27) as i32 - 15 - 9);
                    *t = [
                        (v & 511) as f32 * scale,
                        ((v >> 9) & 511) as f32 * scale,
                        ((v >> 18) & 511) as f32 * scale,
                        1.0,
                    ];
                }
            }
            85 => {
                channels = 3;
                for (i, t) in texels.iter_mut().enumerate() {
                    let v = half(i);
                    *t = [
                        f32::from(v >> 11) / 31.0,
                        f32::from((v >> 5) & 63) / 63.0,
                        f32::from(v & 31) / 31.0,
                        1.0,
                    ];
                }
            }
            86 => {
                channels = 4;
                for (i, t) in texels.iter_mut().enumerate() {
                    let v = half(i);
                    *t = [
                        f32::from((v >> 10) & 31) / 31.0,
                        f32::from((v >> 5) & 31) / 31.0,
                        f32::from(v & 31) / 31.0,
                        f32::from(v >> 15),
                    ];
                }
            }
            115 => {
                channels = 4;
                for (i, t) in texels.iter_mut().enumerate() {
                    let v = half(i);
                    *t = [8, 4, 0, 12].map(|s| f32::from((v >> s) & 15) / 15.0);
                }
            }
            87 | 88 | 91 | 93 => {
                channels = if matches!(format, 87 | 91) { 4 } else { 3 };
                for (i, t) in texels.iter_mut().enumerate() {
                    let [b, g, r, a] = [0, 1, 2, 3].map(|k| f32::from(bytes[i * 4 + k]) / 255.0);
                    *t = [r, g, b, if channels == 4 { a } else { 1.0 }];
                }
            }
            other => return Err(format!("{} cannot be decoded", format::name(other))),
        }
    }
    Ok(Image {
        width,
        height,
        channels,
        float,
        texels,
    })
}

impl Image {
    /// The image as 8-bit RGBA: single-channel images grey, two-channel ones red and green.
    pub fn rgba8(&self, range: Range) -> Vec<u8> {
        let range = match range {
            Range::Auto if self.channels == 1 => {
                let (lo, hi) = self
                    .texels
                    .iter()
                    .map(|t| t[0])
                    .filter(|v| v.is_finite())
                    .fold((f32::MAX, f32::MIN), |(lo, hi), v| (lo.min(v), hi.max(v)));
                if lo < hi {
                    Range::Fixed(lo, hi)
                } else {
                    Range::Clamp
                }
            }
            Range::Auto if self.float => Range::Tonemap,
            Range::Auto => Range::Clamp,
            r => r,
        };
        let map = |v: f32| -> u8 {
            let v = if v.is_nan() { 0.0 } else { v };
            let v = match range {
                Range::Tonemap => {
                    let v = v.max(0.0);
                    v / (1.0 + v)
                }
                Range::Fixed(lo, hi) => (v - lo) / (hi - lo),
                _ => v,
            };
            (v.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * 255.0).round() as u8
        };
        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(self.texels.len() * 4);
        for t in &self.texels {
            let rgb = match self.channels {
                1 => [t[0]; 3],
                2 => [t[0], t[1], 0.0],
                _ => [t[0], t[1], t[2]],
            };
            out.extend(rgb.map(map));
            out.push(if self.channels == 4 {
                (t[3].clamp(0.0, 1.0) * 255.0).round() as u8
            } else {
                255
            });
        }
        out
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn halves() {
        assert_eq!(f16(0x3c00), 1.0);
        assert_eq!(f16(0xc000), -2.0);
        assert_eq!(f16(0x0001), 2f32.powi(-24));
        assert!(f16(0x7c00).is_infinite());
    }

    #[test]
    fn bgra_and_depth() {
        let img = decode(87, 1, 1, &[10, 20, 30, 40]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(img.rgba8(Range::Clamp), vec![30, 20, 10, 40]);
        let depth = decode(46, 2, 1, &[0, 0, 0, 0xab, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(depth.channels, 1);
        assert_eq!(depth.texels[1][0], 1.0);
        assert_eq!(depth.rgba8(Range::Auto), vec![0, 0, 0, 255, 255, 255, 255, 255]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn bc1_solid_block() {
        // Both endpoints pure red (R5G6B5 0xF800), every index 0.
        let block = [0x00, 0xf8, 0x00, 0xf8, 0, 0, 0, 0];
        let img = decode(71, 4, 4, &block).unwrap();
        assert!(
            img.texels
                .iter()
                .all(|t| t[0] == 1.0 && t[1] == 0.0 && t[2] == 0.0)
        );
    }
}
```

`capture/src/writer.rs`:

```rs
//! A background thread for disk writes, so the game's threads hand off blobs and databases instead of waiting on
//! the disk. Jobs run in the order they were given. Blobs in flight are limited to [`BUDGET`] bytes: a caller that
//! must not block (a resource being created) has its blob dropped when the budget is spent, one that can (a capture
//! being written) waits. A key already taken for a store is not taken again, so callers hand over whatever they have
//! without asking the disk first.

use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::mpsc::{Sender, channel};
use std::sync::{Condvar, Mutex, MutexGuard, OnceLock};

use crate::blobs::Blobs;
use crate::cost::Cost;

/// Blobs written (bytes, time on the writer thread), blobs not queued because their key was taken before, blobs
/// dropped because the budget was spent, and blobs whose caller waited for the budget (time waited).
pub static WRITTEN: Cost = Cost::new();
pub static KNOWN: Cost = Cost::new();
pub static DROPPED: Cost = Cost::new();
pub static WAITED: Cost = Cost::new();

/// Keys queued or written, by store root.
static TAKEN: Mutex<Option<HashMap<PathBuf, HashSet<String>>>> = Mutex::new(None);

fn taken() -> MutexGuard<'static, Option<HashMap<PathBuf, HashSet<String>>>> {
    TAKEN.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
}

/// Bytes of blobs that may wait to be written at once.
pub const BUDGET: u64 = 1 << 30;

enum Job {
    Blob(Blobs, String, Vec<u8>),
    Run(Box<dyn FnOnce() + Send>),
}

pub struct Writer {
    tx: Mutex<Sender<Job>>,
    /// Bytes queued, and jobs queued.
    pending: Mutex<(u64, u64)>,
    changed: Condvar,
}

fn writer() -> &'static Writer {
    static WRITER: OnceLock<Writer> = OnceLock::new();
    WRITER.get_or_init(|| {
        let (tx, rx) = channel::<Job>();
        std::thread::Builder::new()
            .name("locum writer".into())
            .spawn(move || {
                for job in rx {
                    let bytes = match job {
                        Job::Blob(blobs, key, data) => {
                            let started = std::time::Instant::now();
                            if blobs.put(&key, &data).is_err() {
                                // Not there after all: the next caller with it queues it again.
                                if let Some(t) = taken().as_mut().and_then(|t| t.get_mut(blobs.root())) {
                                    t.remove(&key);
                                }
                            }
                            WRITTEN.add(started, data.len() as u64);
                            data.len() as u64
                        }
                        Job::Run(f) => {
                            f();
                            0
                        }
                    };
                    let w = writer();
                    let mut p = w.pending.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
                    p.0 -= bytes;
                    p.1 -= 1;
                    w.changed.notify_all();
                }
            })
            .expect("start the writer thread");
        Writer {
            tx: Mutex::new(tx),
            pending: Mutex::new((0, 0)),
            changed: Condvar::new(),
        }
    })
}

fn send(job: Job, bytes: u64) {
    let w = writer();
    {
        let mut p = w.pending.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        p.0 += bytes;
        p.1 += 1;
    }
    let _ = w.tx.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).send(job);
}

/// Queues a blob for writing, unless its key was taken before. With `wait`, blocks while the budget is spent;
/// without, drops the blob and returns false instead. Returns whether the blob is (or will be) in the store.
pub fn blob(blobs: &Blobs, key: String, data: Vec<u8>, wait: bool) -> bool {
    let started = std::time::Instant::now();
    if taken()
        .as_ref()
        .and_then(|t| t.get(blobs.root()))
        .is_some_and(|t| t.contains(&key))
    {
        KNOWN.add(started, data.len() as u64);
        return true;
    }
    let w = writer();
    let bytes = data.len() as u64;
    {
        let mut p = w.pending.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        if p.0 > 0 && p.0 + bytes > BUDGET {
            if !wait {
                DROPPED.add(std::time::Instant::now(), bytes);
                return false;
            }
            let waiting = std::time::Instant::now();
            while p.0 > 0 && p.0 + bytes > BUDGET {
                p = w.changed.wait(p).unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
            }
            WAITED.add(waiting, bytes);
        }
    }
    taken()
        .get_or_insert_with(HashMap::new)
        .entry(blobs.root().to_path_buf())
        .or_default()
        .insert(key.clone());
    send(Job::Blob(blobs.clone(), key, data), bytes);
    true
}

/// Queues `f` to run on the writer thread after everything queued before it.
pub fn run(f: impl FnOnce() + Send + 'static) {
    send(Job::Run(Box::new(f)), 0);
}

/// Waits until everything queued so far is written.
pub fn flush() {
    let w = writer();
    let mut p = w.pending.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    while p.1 > 0 {
        p = w.changed.wait(p).unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn a_key_is_taken_once() {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("locum-writer-test-{}", std::process::id()));
        let blobs = Blobs::new(&dir);
        let key = crate::hash::key(b"once");
        assert!(blob(&blobs, key.clone(), b"once".to_vec(), true));
        flush();
        assert!(blobs.has(&key));
        // Gone from the disk behind the writer's back: the second hand-over is not queued, so it stays gone.
        std::fs::remove_file(blobs.path(&key)).unwrap();
        assert!(blob(&blobs, key.clone(), b"once".to_vec(), true));
        flush();
        assert!(!blobs.has(&key));
        // Another store takes it afresh.
        let other = Blobs::new(dir.join("other"));
        assert!(blob(&other, key.clone(), b"once".to_vec(), true));
        flush();
        assert!(other.has(&key));
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
    }
}
```

```rs
//! Words for what is in a capture: resources, stacks, constants by name.

use std::collections::HashMap;

use locum_capture::format;
use locum_capture::rdef::{self, ConstantBuffer};

use crate::open::Capture;

/// Prints a line to standard output, and leaves quietly when it is closed (piped into `head`).
#[macro_export]
macro_rules! out {
    ($($arg:tt)*) => {{
        use std::io::Write as _;
        if writeln!(std::io::stdout(), $($arg)*).is_err() {
            std::process::exit(0);
        }
    }};
}

/// The order bindings are listed in: input assembly, the shader stages, stream output, output merger.
pub const STAGE_ORDER: &str = "CASE stage WHEN 'ia' THEN 0 WHEN 'vs' THEN 1 WHEN 'hs' THEN 2 WHEN 'ds' THEN 3 \
     WHEN 'gs' THEN 4 WHEN 'so' THEN 5 WHEN 'ps' THEN 6 WHEN 'cs' THEN 7 ELSE 8 END";

/// A resource's shape as the `resources` table has it.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct Shape {
    pub id: i64,
    pub kind: String,
    pub width: u32,
    pub height: u32,
    pub depth: u32,
    pub mips: u32,
    pub array: u32,
    pub format: u32,
    pub samples: u32,
    pub bytes: u64,
    pub stride: u32,
    pub misc: u32,
}

pub const SHAPE_COLUMNS: &str =
    "id, kind, width, height, depth, mips, array, format, samples, bytes, stride, misc";

impl Shape {
    /// From a row whose first columns are [`SHAPE_COLUMNS`].
    pub fn from_row(r: &rusqlite::Row) -> rusqlite::Result<Shape> {
        let n = |i: usize| -> rusqlite::Result<u32> { Ok(r.get::<_, Option<i64>>(i)?.unwrap_or(0) as u32) };
        Ok(Shape {
            id: r.get(0)?,
            kind: r.get(1)?,
            width: n(2)?,
            height: n(3)?,
            depth: n(4)?,
            mips: n(5)?,
            array: n(6)?,
            format: n(7)?,
            samples: n(8)?,
            bytes: r.get::<_, i64>(9)? as u64,
            stride: n(10)?,
            misc: n(11)?,
        })
    }

    pub fn cube(&self) -> bool {
        self.misc & 4 != 0
    }

    /// The subresources of its contents in the canonical layout (as locum laid them out).
    pub fn subs(&self) -> Vec<locum_capture::layout::Sub> {
        if self.kind == "buffer" {
            return locum_capture::layout::buffer(self.width);
        }
        locum_capture::layout::texture(
            self.format,
            self.width,
            self.height,
            self.depth,
            self.mips,
            self.array,
        )
        .unwrap_or_default()
    }
}

impl std::fmt::Display for Shape {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        match self.kind.as_str() {
            "buffer" => {
                write!(f, "#{} buffer {} bytes", self.id, self.width)?;
                if self.stride > 0 {
                    write!(f, " stride {}", self.stride)?;
                }
                Ok(())
            }
            kind => {
                write!(f, "#{} {kind} {}", self.id, self.width)?;
                if kind != "texture1d" {
                    write!(f, "x{}", self.height)?;
                }
                if kind == "texture3d" {
                    write!(f, "x{}", self.depth)?;
                }
                write!(f, " {}", format::name(self.format))?;
                if self.mips > 1 {
                    write!(f, " {} mips", self.mips)?;
                }
                if self.cube() {
                    write!(f, " cube")?;
                    if self.array > 6 {
                        write!(f, " x{}", self.array / 6)?;
                    }
                } else if self.array > 1 {
                    write!(f, " [{}]", self.array)?;
                }
                if self.samples > 1 {
                    write!(f, " {}x MSAA", self.samples)?;
                }
                Ok(())
            }
        }
    }
}

pub fn shape(c: &Capture, id: i64) -> Option<Shape> {
    c.row(
        &format!("SELECT {SHAPE_COLUMNS} FROM resources WHERE id = ?1"),
        [id],
        Shape::from_row,
    )
}

/// A stack's frames as `module+0xoffset`, innermost first.
pub fn stack(c: &Capture, id: i64) -> Vec<String> {
    let Some(frames) = c.row("SELECT frames FROM stacks WHERE id = ?1", [id], |r| {
        r.get::<_, Vec<u8>>(0)
    }) else {
        return Vec::new();
    };
    let modules: Vec<(String, u64, u64)> = c.rows("SELECT path, base, size FROM modules", [], |r| {
        Ok((r.get(0)?, r.get::<_, i64>(1)? as u64, r.get::<_, i64>(2)? as u64))
    });
    frames
        .as_chunks::<8>()
        .0
        .iter()
        .map(|&b| {
            let a = u64::from_le_bytes(b);
            match modules
                .iter()
                .find(|(_, base, size)| (*base..base + size).contains(&a))
            {
                Some((path, base, _)) => {
                    let name = path.rsplit(['\\', '/']).next().unwrap_or(path);
                    format!("{name}+0x{:x}", a - base)
                }
                None => format!("0x{a:x}"),
            }
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Shader reflection by shader hash, read once.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Reflection {
    cache: HashMap<String, Option<Vec<ConstantBuffer>>>,
}

impl Reflection {
    /// The constant buffer a shader declares at register `slot` (space `space`).
    pub fn cb<'a>(
        &'a mut self,
        c: &Capture,
        shader: &str,
        slot: u32,
        space: u32,
    ) -> Option<&'a ConstantBuffer> {
        let cbs = self.cache.entry(shader.to_string()).or_insert_with(|| {
            let key: String = c.row(
                "SELECT blob FROM shaders WHERE hash = ?1 AND blob IS NOT NULL",
                [shader],
                |r| r.get(0),
            )?;
            rdef::constant_buffers(&c.blob(&key).ok()?)
        });
        cbs.as_ref()?
            .iter()
            .find(|b| b.slot == Some(slot) && b.space == space)
    }
}

/// A 4-byte constant as its type says (float when unknown), at most 12 characters.
pub fn value(bytes: [u8; 4], base: Option<u16>) -> String {
    match base {
        Some(1) => (u32::from_le_bytes(bytes) != 0).to_string(),
        Some(2) => i32::from_le_bytes(bytes).to_string(),
        Some(19 | 20) => u32::from_le_bytes(bytes).to_string(),
        _ => float(f32::from_le_bytes(bytes)),
    }
}

/// A float in at most 12 characters: plainly when it fits, else in exponent form; denormals and NaNs (more likely
/// integers or packed bits) as hex.
pub fn float(f: f32) -> String {
    let bits = f.to_bits();
    if (f != 0.0 && f.abs() < 1e-30) || f.is_nan() {
        return format!("0x{bits:08x}");
    }
    let a = f.abs();
    let plain = format!("{f}");
    if plain.len() <= 12 && a < 1e7 {
        return plain;
    }
    if (1e-4..1e7).contains(&a) {
        // Round to fit: the integer digits, the point and as many decimals as are left.
        let digits = (a.log10().floor() as i32 + 1).max(1) as usize;
        let sign = usize::from(f < 0.0);
        let decimals = 12usize.saturating_sub(digits + 1 + sign).min(9);
        return format!("{f:.decimals$}");
    }
    format!("{f:.4e}")
}

/// The names of a register's four components, shortened to `name` when they are `name.x` to `name.w`.
pub fn register_name(names: &[Option<String>; 4]) -> String {
    if let Some(Some(first)) = names.first()
        && let Some(base) = first.strip_suffix(".x")
        && names
            .iter()
            .zip(["x", "y", "z", "w"])
            .all(|(n, c)| n.as_deref() == Some(&format!("{base}.{c}")))
    {
        return base.to_string();
    }
    let mut distinct: Vec<&str> = Vec::new();
    for n in names.iter().flatten() {
        if !distinct.contains(&n.as_str()) {
            distinct.push(n);
        }
    }
    distinct.join(" ")
}

/// Short key for tables.
pub fn short(key: &str) -> &str {
    key.get(..12).unwrap_or(key)
}

/// A count of bytes in MiB with one decimal.
pub fn mib(bytes: u64) -> String {
    format!("{:.1} MiB", bytes as f64 / (1 << 20) as f64)
}
```
