```rs
            "resolve" => {
                let (d, s) = (
                    self.resource(json_u32(&a, "dst") as i64)?.clone(),
                    self.resource(json_u32(&a, "src") as i64)?.clone(),
                );
                unsafe {
                    ctx.ResolveSubresource(
                        &d,
                        json_u32(&a, "dst_sub"),
                        &s,
                        json_u32(&a, "src_sub"),
                        DXGI_FORMAT(json_u32(&a, "format") as i32),
                    )
                };
            }
            "mips" => {
                if let Some(v) = self.srv(c, Some(json_u32(&a, "view") as i64))? {
                    unsafe { ctx.GenerateMips(&v) };
                }
            }
            "copy_count" => {
                let d = self.buffer(json_u32(&a, "dst") as i64)?;
                if let Some(v) = self.uav(c, json_u32(&a, "view") as i64)? {
                    unsafe { ctx.CopyStructureCount(&d, json_u32(&a, "offset"), &v) };
                }
            }
            "uav_counter" => {
                for s in a["set"].as_array().into_iter().flatten() {
                    let Some(v) = self.uav(c, json_u32(s, "view") as i64)? else {
                        continue;
                    };
                    let count = json_u32(s, "count");
                    let slot = json_u32(s, "slot");
                    unsafe {
                        if call.starts_with("CS") {
                            ctx.CSSetUnorderedAccessViews(slot, 1, Some(&Some(v)), Some(&count));
                        } else {
                            // The next draw binds its own targets again; the counter stays with the view.
                            ctx.OMSetRenderTargetsAndUnorderedAccessViews(
                                None,
                                None,
                                slot,
                                1,
                                Some(&Some(v)),
                                Some(&count),
                            );
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            // Discards leave contents undefined; keeping them is one valid outcome. Map starts and reads change
            // nothing on the GPU.
            "discard" | "map_begin" | "map_read" => {}
            other => self.warn(format!("events of kind {other} are not replayed")),
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn read(&mut self, id: i64) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
        let r = self.resource(id)?.clone();
        let ctx: ID3D11DeviceContext = self.ctx.cast().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        let rb = unsafe { locum_d3d11::readback::issue(&ctx, &r) }?;
        unsafe { rb.read(&ctx) }
    }

    fn write(&mut self, c: &Capture, id: i64, contents: &[u8]) -> Result<(), String> {
        let s = shape(c, id).ok_or("not described in the capture")?;
        let subs = s.subs();
        if contents.len() as u64 != layout::total(&subs) {
            return Err(format!(
                "#{id}: {} bytes do not fit its {} bytes of subresources",
                contents.len(),
                layout::total(&subs)
            ));
        }
        let r = self.resource(id)?.clone();
        for x in &subs {
            unsafe {
                self.ctx.UpdateSubresource(
                    &r,
                    x.index,
                    None,
                    contents[x.offset as usize..].as_ptr().cast(),
                    x.row_bytes,
                    x.row_bytes * x.rows,
                )
            };
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn warnings(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        let mut warnings = self.warnings.clone();
        if let Some(queue) = &self.debug {
            unsafe {
                if queue.GetNumMessagesDiscardedByMessageCountLimit() != 0 {
                    warnings.insert("D3D11 validation messages were lost to the queue limit".into());
                }
                for i in 0..queue.GetNumStoredMessagesAllowedByRetrievalFilter() {
                    let mut size = 0;
                    if let Err(e) = queue.GetMessage(i, None, &mut size) {
                        warnings.insert(format!("D3D11 validation message {i}: {e}"));
                        continue;
                    }
                    // The queue writes a D3D11_MESSAGE followed by its text; keep the header aligned.
                    let mut storage = vec![0usize; size.div_ceil(size_of::<usize>())];
                    let message = storage.as_mut_ptr().cast::<D3D11_MESSAGE>();
                    if let Err(e) = queue.GetMessage(i, Some(message), &mut size) {
                        warnings.insert(format!("D3D11 validation message {i}: {e}"));
                        continue;
                    }
                    let message = &*message;
                    if matches!(
                        message.Severity,
                        D3D11_MESSAGE_SEVERITY_ERROR | D3D11_MESSAGE_SEVERITY_CORRUPTION
                    ) {
                        let text =
                            std::slice::from_raw_parts(message.pDescription, message.DescriptionByteLength);
                        warnings.insert(format!(
                            "D3D11 validation: {}",
                            String::from_utf8_lossy(text).trim_end_matches('\0')
                        ));
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        warnings.into_iter().collect()
    }
}

```

`cli/src/replay/mod.rs`:

```rs
//! Replaying a captured frame offline, with or without rules changing it. What runs is planned here from the capture
//! alone (API-neutral); a backend for the capture's API makes the resources and runs the events
//! ([`d3d11`] for Direct3D 11).
//!
//! A draw is replayed with what it depends on: walking back from it, every earlier event that wrote something it (or
//! an event already taken) reads or writes is taken too, so the resources it sees hold what they held in the game.
//! Resources start with their contents as the frame began.

mod d3d11;

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet, HashMap};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use locum_capture::format;
use locum_capture::rules::{self, Rule};
use locum_capture::texels::{self, Range};

use crate::describe::{Shape, mib, shape};
use crate::export::png;
use crate::open::Capture;
use crate::out;

/// What a backend for one graphics API does.
pub trait Backend {
    /// Makes resource `id` as the capture describes it, holding `contents` (the canonical layout) if given.
    fn create(&mut self, c: &Capture, id: i64, contents: Option<&[u8]>) -> Result<(), String>;
    /// Runs event `seq` as the capture recorded it, draws and dispatches with `rules` applied.
    fn run(&mut self, c: &Capture, seq: i64, rules: &[Rule]) -> Result<(), String>;
    /// Resource `id`'s contents now, in the canonical layout.
    fn read(&mut self, id: i64) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String>;
    /// Replaces resource `id`'s contents with `contents` (the canonical layout).
    fn write(&mut self, c: &Capture, id: i64, contents: &[u8]) -> Result<(), String>;
    /// What it could not do as recorded, once each.
    fn warnings(&self) -> Vec<String>;
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub enum Mode {
    /// The draw and the earlier events it depends on.
    Slice,
    /// Every event up to the draw.
    Frame,
    /// The draw alone, on contents as the frame began.
    Draw,
}

impl Mode {
    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Option<Mode> {
        match s {
            "slice" => Some(Mode::Slice),
            "frame" => Some(Mode::Frame),
            "draw" => Some(Mode::Draw),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

/// The resources an event reads and writes. A draw's constant buffers are not among its reads: replay binds the
/// bytes the GPU read, captured at the draw.
fn touches(c: &Capture) -> BTreeMap<i64, (BTreeSet<i64>, BTreeSet<i64>)> {
    let mut out: BTreeMap<i64, (BTreeSet<i64>, BTreeSet<i64>)> = BTreeMap::new();
    for seq in c.rows("SELECT seq FROM events", [], |r| r.get::<_, i64>(0)) {
        out.insert(seq, Default::default());
    }
    for (event, resource, access) in c.rows("SELECT event, resource, access FROM event_resources", [], |r| {
        Ok((r.get::<_, i64>(0)?, r.get::<_, i64>(1)?, r.get::<_, String>(2)?))
    }) {
        let e = out.entry(event).or_default();
        if access == "write" {
            e.1.insert(resource);
        } else {
            e.0.insert(resource);
        }
    }
    // Drop reads that are only constant buffers of the draw.
    let cb_only: Vec<(i64, i64)> = c.rows(
        "SELECT d.event, b.resource FROM bindings b JOIN draws d ON d.n = b.draw WHERE b.resource IS NOT NULL \
         GROUP BY d.event, b.resource HAVING sum(b.kind <> 'cb') = 0",
        [],
        |r| Ok((r.get(0)?, r.get(1)?)),
    );
    for (event, resource) in cb_only {
        if let Some(e) = out.get_mut(&event) {
            e.0.remove(&resource);
        }
    }
    out
}

pub struct Plan {
    pub events: Vec<i64>,
    pub resources: BTreeSet<i64>,
}

/// The events to run to replay event `target`, and the resources they touch.
pub fn plan(c: &Capture, target: i64, mode: Mode) -> Plan {
    let touches = touches(c);
    let mut events: Vec<i64> = Vec::new();
    let mut resources: BTreeSet<i64> = BTreeSet::new();
    let mut take = |seq: i64, resources: &mut BTreeSet<i64>| {
        if let Some((r, w)) = touches.get(&seq) {
            resources.extend(r);
            resources.extend(w);
        }
        events.push(seq);
    };
    match mode {
        Mode::Draw => take(target, &mut resources),
        Mode::Frame => {
            for &seq in touches.keys().filter(|&&s| s <= target) {
                take(seq, &mut resources);
            }
        }
        Mode::Slice => {
            take(target, &mut resources);
            for (&seq, (_, writes)) in touches.range(..target).rev() {
                if writes.iter().any(|w| resources.contains(w)) {
                    take(seq, &mut resources);
                }
            }
            events.reverse();
        }
    }
    // Everything a draw has bound, and the resource of every view an event names, in one query (one per event
    // scans the bindings once per event: minutes on a game's frame).
    let mut bound: BTreeMap<i64, Vec<i64>> = BTreeMap::new();
    for (event, resource) in c.rows(
        "SELECT DISTINCT d.event, b.resource FROM bindings b JOIN draws d ON d.n = b.draw \
         WHERE b.resource IS NOT NULL AND b.kind <> 'cb'",
        [],
        |r| Ok((r.get::<_, i64>(0)?, r.get::<_, i64>(1)?)),
    ) {
        bound.entry(event).or_default().push(resource);
    }
    for seq in &events {
        if let Some(b) = bound.get(seq) {
            resources.extend(b);
        }
    }
    Plan { events, resources }
}

/// One output of a draw: a target or UAV and the subresource of its resource it covers.
struct Output {
    name: String,
    resource: i64,
    sub: Option<u32>,
}

fn outputs(c: &Capture, draw: i64) -> Vec<Output> {
    c.rows(
        "SELECT b.kind, b.slot, b.resource, v.json FROM bindings b LEFT JOIN views v ON v.id = b.view \
         WHERE b.draw = ?1 AND b.kind IN ('rtv', 'dsv', 'uav') AND b.resource IS NOT NULL ORDER BY b.kind DESC, b.slot",
        [draw],
        |r| {
            Ok((
                r.get::<_, String>(0)?,
                r.get::<_, i64>(1)?,
                r.get::<_, i64>(2)?,
                r.get::<_, Option<String>>(3)?,
            ))
        },
    )
    .into_iter()
    .map(|(kind, slot, resource, json)| {
        let name = match kind.as_str() {
            "rtv" => format!("rt{slot}"),
            "dsv" => "depth".into(),
            _ => format!("u{slot}"),
        };
        let range = json
            .and_then(|j| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&j).ok())
            .map(|j| j["range"].clone())
            .unwrap_or_default();
        let sub = shape(c, resource).and_then(|s| {
            (s.kind != "buffer").then(|| {
                let mip = range["mip"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0) as u32;
                let slice = range["first_slice"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0) as u32;
                mip + slice * s.mips.max(1)
            })
        });
        Output {
            name,
            resource,
            sub,
        }
    })
    .collect()
}

/// A subresource's bytes and shape out of a resource's canonical contents.
fn sub_of<'a>(
    s: &Shape,
    bytes: &'a [u8],
    sub: Option<u32>,
) -> Option<(&'a [u8], locum_capture::layout::Sub)> {
    let subs = s.subs();
    let x = *subs.iter().find(|x| Some(x.index) == sub.or(Some(0)))?;
    Some((bytes.get(x.offset as usize..(x.offset + x.size) as usize)?, x))
}

/// How two images of the same format differ: texels that differ, of how many, the largest difference in a decoded
/// channel, and the box holding the differing texels.
struct Difference {
    differ: u64,
    total: u64,
    largest: f32,
    bounds: Option<(u32, u32, u32, u32)>,
}

fn compare(format: u32, sub: &locum_capture::layout::Sub, a: &[u8], b: &[u8]) -> Difference {
    let block = format::layout(format)
        .map_or(4, |l| l.block_bytes as usize)
        .max(1);
    let (bw, bh) = format::layout(format).map_or((1, 1), |l| (l.block_width, l.block_height));
    let per_row = (sub.row_bytes as usize / block).max(1);
    let mut d = Difference {
        differ: 0,
        total: (a.len() / block) as u64,
        largest: 0.0,
        bounds: None,
    };
    for (i, (x, y)) in a.chunks(block).zip(b.chunks(block)).enumerate() {
        if x != y {
            d.differ += 1;
            let (px, py) = (
                (i % per_row) as u32 * bw,
                ((i / per_row) % sub.rows as usize) as u32 * bh,
            );
            d.bounds = Some(match d.bounds {
                None => (px, py, px + bw, py + bh),
                Some((l, t, r, btm)) => (l.min(px), t.min(py), r.max(px + bw), btm.max(py + bh)),
            });
        }
    }
    if d.differ > 0
        && let (Ok(ia), Ok(ib)) = (
            texels::decode(format, sub.width, sub.height, a),
            texels::decode(format, sub.width, sub.height, b),
        )
    {
        for (x, y) in ia.texels.iter().zip(&ib.texels) {
            for k in 0..4 {
                let diff = (x[k] - y[k]).abs();
                if diff.is_finite() {
                    d.largest = d.largest.max(diff);
                }
            }
        }
    }
    d
}

impl std::fmt::Display for Difference {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        if self.differ == 0 {
            return write!(f, "identical");
        }
        write!(
            f,
            "{} of {} texels differ ({:.3}%), largest channel difference {}",
            self.differ,
            self.total,
            self.differ as f64 * 100.0 / self.total.max(1) as f64,
            self.largest
        )?;
        if let Some((l, t, r, b)) = self.bounds {
            write!(f, ", within x {l}..{r} y {t}..{b}")?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// A picture of where two images differ: unchanged texels dim grey, changed ones as they are now tinted magenta, so a
/// change to black still shows.
fn diff_png(
    path: &Path,
    format: u32,
    sub: &locum_capture::layout::Sub,
    before: &[u8],
    after: &[u8],
    range: Range,
) -> Result<(), String> {
    let a = texels::decode(format, sub.width, sub.height, before)?;
    let b = texels::decode(format, sub.width, sub.height, after)?;
    let (pa, pb) = (a.rgba8(range), b.rgba8(range));
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(pb.len());
    for (x, y) in pa.chunks(4).zip(pb.chunks(4)) {
        if x == y {
            let grey = ((u16::from(y[0]) + u16::from(y[1]) + u16::from(y[2])) / 12) as u8;
            out.extend([grey, grey, grey, 255]);
        } else {
            let tint = |c: u8, t: u16| ((u16::from(c) + t) / 2) as u8;
            out.extend([tint(y[0], 255), tint(y[1], 0), tint(y[2], 255), 255]);
        }
    }
    png(path, sub.width, sub.height, &out)
}

fn write_output(
    dir: &Path,
    name: &str,
    s: &Shape,
    bytes: &[u8],
    sub: Option<u32>,
    range: Range,
) -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
    if s.kind == "buffer" {
        let path = dir.join(format!("{name}.bin"));
        std::fs::write(&path, bytes).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", path.display()))?;
        return Ok(path);
    }
    let (data, x) = sub_of(s, bytes, sub).ok_or("no such subresource")?;
    let path = dir.join(format!("{name}.png"));
    let image = texels::decode(s.format, x.width, x.height, &data[..x.slice_bytes() as usize])?;
    png(&path, x.width, x.height, &image.rgba8(range))?;
    Ok(path)
}

/// Makes the plan's resources on a new backend and runs its events with `rules`; returns each output's contents.
fn execute(
    c: &Capture,
    plan: &Plan,
    rules: &[Rule],
    warp: bool,
    debug: bool,
    outs: &[Output],
) -> Result<(Vec<Vec<u8>>, Vec<String>), String> {
    let mut b = backend(c, warp, debug)?;
    let mut missing = 0;
    for &id in &plan.resources {
        let key: Option<String> = c
            .row("SELECT content FROM resources WHERE id = ?1", [id], |r| r.get(0))
            .flatten();
        let contents = match key {
            Some(k) => Some(c.blob(&k)?),
            None => {
                missing += 1;
                None
            }
        };
        b.create(c, id, contents.as_deref())
            .map_err(|e| format!("resource #{id}: {e}"))?;
    }
    // Only order-dependent outputs are put back: the game's bytes for any other would undo what a rule changed.
    let written = recorded(c);
    let mut settled = 0;
    for &seq in &plan.events {
        b.run(c, seq, rules).map_err(|e| format!("event {seq}: {e}"))?;
        settled += settle(c, b.as_mut(), &written, seq, false)
            .map_err(|e| format!("event {seq}: {e}"))?
            .iter()
            .filter(|s| s.ordered)
            .count();
    }
    let mut results = Vec::new();
    for o in outs {
        results.push(b.read(o.resource)?);
    }
    let mut warnings = b.warnings();
    if missing > 0 {
        warnings.push(format!(
            "{missing} resources had no contents in the capture and started empty"
        ));
    }
    if settled > 0 && !rules.is_empty() {
        warnings.push(format!(
            "{settled} outputs of order-dependent draws and dispatches are the game's, so rules do not change them"
        ));
    }
    Ok((results, warnings))
}

/// What the game's GPU wrote through a UAV in a draw or dispatch, recorded right after it.
struct Written {
    resource: i64,
    key: String,
    /// One of its shaders writes what depends on the order the GPU runs its threads.
    ordered: bool,
}

/// What the game's GPU wrote through UAVs in each draw and dispatch, by event. Captures from before every output was
/// recorded hold only order-dependent ones, without the column saying so; older ones have none.
fn recorded(c: &Capture) -> HashMap<i64, Vec<Written>> {
    let mut out: HashMap<i64, Vec<Written>> = HashMap::new();
    let columns: Vec<String> = c.rows("SELECT name FROM pragma_table_info('results')", [], |r| r.get(0));
    if columns.is_empty() {
        return out;
    }
    let ordered = if columns.iter().any(|n| n == "order_dependent") {
        "order_dependent"
    } else {
        "1"
    };
    for (event, w) in c.rows(
        &format!("SELECT event, resource, content, {ordered} FROM results"),
        [],
        |r| {
            Ok((
                r.get::<_, i64>(0)?,
                Written {
                    resource: r.get(1)?,
                    key: r.get(2)?,
                    ordered: r.get(3)?,
                },
            ))
        },
    ) {
        out.entry(event).or_default().push(w);
    }
    out
}

/// How an event's output in replay compares with the game's.
enum Settled {
    Identical,
    /// The same records, `stride` bytes each, in another order.
    Reordered {
        stride: usize,
    },
    Differs(String),
}

/// One output of an event, compared.
struct Compared {
    resource: i64,
    ordered: bool,
    settled: Settled,
}

/// After event `seq` ran, compares what it wrote through UAVs with what the game's GPU wrote. Where they differ, the
/// game's bytes are put in place for order-dependent outputs always, and for every output when `all`: everything
/// after then follows the order the game's GPU took, and starts from the game's state, so a difference later is that
/// later event's own. An order-dependent output can hold the same records in another order, or differ in more than
/// order: a shader that writes what its atomics returned (an offset into a list it allocates from, say) writes other
/// values when its threads run in another order. Any other output is identical or differs.
fn settle(
    c: &Capture,
    b: &mut dyn Backend,
    written: &HashMap<i64, Vec<Written>>,
    seq: i64,
    all: bool,
) -> Result<Vec<Compared>, String> {
    let Some(written) = written.get(&seq) else {
        return Ok(Vec::new());
    };
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for w in written {
        let s = shape(c, w.resource).ok_or("resource vanished")?;
        let game = c.blob(&w.key)?;
        let mine = b.read(w.resource)?;
        // A structured buffer's records are its structures; anything else is taken in 4-byte words, the unit UAV
        // atomics work in.
        let stride = if s.kind == "buffer" && s.stride > 0 {
            s.stride as usize
        } else {
            4
        };
        let settled = if mine == game {
            Settled::Identical
        } else if mine.len() != game.len() {
            Settled::Differs(format!("{} bytes, the game's {}", mine.len(), game.len()))
        } else if w.ordered
            && s.kind == "buffer"
            && game.len() % stride == 0
            && same_records(&mine, &game, stride)
        {
            Settled::Reordered { stride }
        } else {
            let differ = mine
                .chunks(stride)
                .zip(game.chunks(stride))
                .filter(|(a, g)| a != g)
                .count();
            Settled::Differs(format!(
                "{differ} of {} {stride}-byte records differ",
                game.len().div_ceil(stride)
            ))
        };
        if !matches!(settled, Settled::Identical) && (w.ordered || all) {
            b.write(c, w.resource, &game)?;
        }
        out.push(Compared {
            resource: w.resource,
            ordered: w.ordered,
            settled,
        });
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// Whether `a` and `b` hold the same `stride`-byte records, as many times each, in any order.
fn same_records(a: &[u8], b: &[u8], stride: usize) -> bool {
    let mut x: Vec<&[u8]> = a.chunks_exact(stride).collect();
    let mut y: Vec<&[u8]> = b.chunks_exact(stride).collect();
    x.sort_unstable();
    y.sort_unstable();
    x == y
}

fn backend(c: &Capture, warp: bool, debug: bool) -> Result<Box<dyn Backend>, String> {
    match c.meta("api").as_deref() {
        Some("d3d11") => Ok(Box::new(d3d11::D3d11::new(warp, debug)?)),
        other => Err(format!("no replay for API {other:?}")),
    }
}

/// The draw named on the command line: a number, or `last`.
pub fn draw_number(c: &Capture, arg: &str) -> Result<i64, String> {
    if arg == "last" {
        return c
            .row("SELECT max(n) FROM draws", [], |r| r.get::<_, Option<i64>>(0))
            .flatten()
            .ok_or_else(|| "the capture has no draws".into());
    }
    arg.parse()
        .map_err(|_| format!("{arg:?} is not a draw number or `last`"))
}

pub struct Options {
    pub mode: Mode,
    pub rules: Vec<String>,
    pub rules_file: Option<PathBuf>,
    pub warp: bool,
    pub debug: bool,
    pub out: PathBuf,
    pub range: Range,
}

/// The shader a rule names, by its hash or the start of it, among the capture's shaders of that stage: a hash that
/// names none of them, or more than one, is an error rather than a rule that never applies.
fn shader_named(c: &Capture, stage: usize, hash: &str) -> Result<u64, String> {
    let name = rules::STAGES[stage];
    if hash.is_empty() || !hash.chars().all(|ch| ch.is_ascii_hexdigit()) {
        return Err(format!("{hash:?} is not a hex hash"));
    }
    let found: Vec<String> = c.rows(
        "SELECT hash FROM shaders WHERE stage = ?1 AND hash LIKE ?2 || '%' ORDER BY hash LIMIT 3",
        (name, hash.to_ascii_lowercase()),
        |r| r.get(0),
    );
    match found.as_slice() {
        [one] => u64::from_str_radix(one, 16).map_err(|_| format!("{one:?} is not a hex hash")),
        [] => Err(format!("the capture has no {name} shader {hash}")),
        [a, b, ..] => Err(format!(
            "{name}={hash} names more than one shader ({a}, {b}): give more of the hash"
        )),
    }
}

pub fn replay(c: &Capture, draw: i64, o: &Options) -> Result<(), String> {
    let target: i64 = c
        .row("SELECT event FROM draws WHERE n = ?1", [draw], |r| r.get(0))
        .ok_or_else(|| format!("no draw {draw}"))?;
    let mut parsed = Vec::new();
    if let Some(file) = &o.rules_file {
        let text = std::fs::read_to_string(file).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", file.display()))?;
        let dir = file.parent().unwrap_or(Path::new("."));
        let (r, errors) = rules::parse_all(&text, dir, &|stage, hash| shader_named(c, stage, hash));
        if let Some((line, e)) = errors.first() {
            return Err(format!("{} line {line}: {e}", file.display()));
        }
        parsed.extend(r);
    }
    for text in &o.rules {
        parsed.push(rules::parse(text, Path::new("."), &|stage, hash| {
            shader_named(c, stage, hash)
        })?);
    }
    let plan = plan(c, target, o.mode);
    let bytes: u64 = plan
        .resources
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|&id| shape(c, id))
        .map(|s| s.bytes)
        .sum();
    out!(
        "replaying draw {draw} (event {target}): {} events, {} resources ({}){}",
        plan.events.len(),
        plan.resources.len(),
        mib(bytes),
        if o.warp { " on WARP" } else { "" }
    );
    if o.mode == Mode::Draw {
        let earlier: Vec<i64> = c.rows(
            "SELECT DISTINCT resource FROM event_resources WHERE access = 'write' AND event < ?1",
            [target],
            |r| r.get(0),
        );
        let stale: Vec<String> = plan
            .resources
            .iter()
            .filter(|r| earlier.contains(r))
            .map(|r| format!("#{r}"))
            .collect();
        if !stale.is_empty() {
            out!(
                "  note: {} were written earlier in the frame; this draw sees them as the frame began",
                stale.join(" ")
            );
        }
    }
    let outs = outputs(c, draw);
    if outs.is_empty() {
        return Err(format!("draw {draw} has no targets or UAVs to show"));
    }
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&o.out).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", o.out.display()))?;
    let t = std::time::Instant::now();
    let (base, warnings) = execute(c, &plan, &[], o.warp, o.debug, &outs)?;
    out!("  replayed in {:.2} s", t.elapsed().as_secs_f64());
    for w in &warnings {
        out!("  warning: {w}");
    }
    let edited = if parsed.is_empty() {
        None
    } else {
        let (after, _) = execute(c, &plan, &parsed, o.warp, o.debug, &outs)?;
        Some(after)
    };
    // Captured targets after this draw, to compare the replay against.
    let captured: HashMap<String, String> = c
        .rows(
            "SELECT target, blob FROM targets WHERE draw = ?1 AND blob IS NOT NULL",
            [draw],
            |r| Ok((r.get(0)?, r.get(1)?)),
        )
        .into_iter()
        .collect();
    for (i, output) in outs.iter().enumerate() {
        let s = shape(c, output.resource).ok_or("resource vanished")?;
        let suffix = if edited.is_some() { ".before" } else { "" };
        let path = write_output(
            &o.out,
            &format!("{}{suffix}", output.name),
            &s,
            &base[i],
            output.sub,
            o.range,
        )?;
        out!("{}: {s} -> {}", output.name, path.display());
        if s.kind == "buffer" {
            continue;
        }
        let Some((now, x)) = sub_of(&s, &base[i], output.sub) else {
            continue;
        };
        let fmt = format::readable(s.format);
        if let Some(key) = captured.get(&output.name)
            && let Ok(game) = c.blob(key)
        {
            out!("  against the game's: {}", compare(fmt, &x, &game, now));
        }
        if let Some(after) = &edited {
            let Some((then, _)) = sub_of(&s, &after[i], output.sub) else {
                continue;
            };
            let p = write_output(
                &o.out,
                &format!("{}.after", output.name),
                &s,
                &after[i],
                output.sub,
                o.range,
            )?;
            let d = o.out.join(format!("{}.diff.png", output.name));
            diff_png(&d, fmt, &x, now, then, o.range)?;
            out!(
                "  with the rules: {} -> {}, {}",
                compare(fmt, &x, now, then),
                p.display(),
                d.display()
            );
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Gaps that are checks the capture could not make or keep (targets not read back, a command list's earlier
/// executions, the CPU's memory), not inputs the replay lacks: shown, but they leave the proof complete.
const CHECKS: &str = "'evidence', 'targets', 'outputs', 'memory'";

/// Replays the whole frame and compares every target the capture read back with the replay's at the same point. Fails
/// unless every target compared is identical and nothing kept the capture or the replay from being complete.
pub fn verify(c: &Capture, warp: bool, debug: bool, limit: Option<i64>) -> Result<(), String> {
    let last: i64 = c
        .row("SELECT max(seq) FROM events", [], |r| r.get::<_, Option<i64>>(0))
        .flatten()
        .ok_or("the capture has no events")?;
    let started = std::time::Instant::now();
    let plan = plan(c, last, Mode::Frame);
    let planned = started.elapsed();
    // Each target is compared after the event it was read after (in captures from before that was recorded, its draw).
    let has_event = c
        .row(
            "SELECT count(*) FROM pragma_table_info('targets') WHERE name = 'event'",
            [],
            |r| r.get::<_, i64>(0),
        )
        .is_some_and(|n| n > 0);
    let at = if has_event {
        "coalesce(t.event, d.event)"
    } else {
        "d.event"
    };
    let checks: Vec<(i64, i64, String, i64, String, i64)> = c.rows(
        &format!(
            "SELECT t.draw, {at} AS at, t.target, t.resource, t.blob, coalesce(t.sub, 0) FROM targets t \
             JOIN draws d ON d.n = t.draw WHERE t.blob IS NOT NULL AND t.resource IS NOT NULL ORDER BY at"
        ),
        [],
        |r| Ok((r.get(0)?, r.get(1)?, r.get(2)?, r.get(3)?, r.get(4)?, r.get(5)?)),
    );
    out!(
        "replaying {} events over {} resources; {} targets to compare",
        plan.events.len(),
        plan.resources.len(),
        checks.len()
    );
    let started = std::time::Instant::now();
    let mut b = backend(c, warp, debug)?;
    for &id in &plan.resources {
        let key: Option<String> = c
            .row("SELECT content FROM resources WHERE id = ?1", [id], |r| r.get(0))
            .flatten();
        let contents = match key {
            Some(k) => Some(c.blob(&k)?),
            None => None,
        };
        b.create(c, id, contents.as_deref())
            .map_err(|e| format!("resource #{id}: {e}"))?;
    }
    out!(
        "planned in {:.1} s; device and resources made in {:.1} s",
        planned.as_secs_f64(),
        started.elapsed().as_secs_f64()
    );
    let written = recorded(c);
    // Draws and dispatches are named by their number, as targets are.
    let numbered: HashMap<i64, (i64, String)> = c
        .rows("SELECT event, n, call FROM draws", [], |r| {
            Ok((r.get::<_, i64>(0)?, (r.get::<_, i64>(1)?, r.get::<_, String>(2)?)))
        })
        .into_iter()
        .collect();
    let mut next = 0;
    let (mut same, mut compared) = (0, 0);
    let (mut settled_same, mut reordered, mut differing) = (0, 0, 0);
    let (mut outputs_same, mut outputs_differing) = (0, 0);
    let t = std::time::Instant::now();
    for &seq in &plan.events {
        b.run(c, seq, &[]).map_err(|e| format!("event {seq}: {e}"))?;
        let who = numbered.get(&seq).map_or_else(
            || format!("event {seq}"),
            |(n, call)| format!("{call} {n} (event {seq})"),
        );
        for out in settle(c, b.as_mut(), &written, seq, true).map_err(|e| format!("event {seq}: {e}"))? {
            let resource = out.resource;
            match (out.ordered, out.settled) {
                (true, Settled::Identical) => settled_same += 1,
                (false, Settled::Identical) => outputs_same += 1,
                (_, Settled::Reordered { stride }) => {
                    reordered += 1;
                    out!(
                        "{who} #{resource}: the game's {stride}-byte records in another order; going on from the \
                         game's order"
                    );
                }
                (true, Settled::Differs(how)) => {
                    differing += 1;
                    out!(
                        "{who} #{resource}: order-dependent, differs from the game's output in more than order \
                         ({how}); going on from the game's"
                    );
                }
                (false, Settled::Differs(how)) => {
                    outputs_differing += 1;
                    out!(
                        "{who} #{resource}: wrote other bytes than the game's ({how}); going on from the game's"
                    );
                }
            }
        }
        while next < checks.len() && checks[next].1 == seq {
            let (draw, _, name, resource, key, sub) = &checks[next];
            next += 1;
            if limit.is_some_and(|l| compared >= l) {
                continue;
            }
            let s = shape(c, *resource).ok_or("resource vanished")?;
            let now = b.read(*resource)?;
            let Some((mine, x)) = sub_of(&s, &now, Some(*sub as u32)) else {
                continue;
            };
            let game = c.blob(key)?;
            let d = compare(format::readable(s.format), &x, &game, mine);
            compared += 1;
            if d.differ == 0 {
                same += 1;
            }
            out!("draw {draw:>5} {name:<6} {s}: {d}");
        }
    }
    out!(
        "{same} of {compared} targets identical; replayed in {:.1} s",
        t.elapsed().as_secs_f64()
    );
    if outputs_same + outputs_differing > 0 {
        out!(
            "what draws and dispatches wrote through UAVs: {outputs_same} identical to the game's, {outputs_differing} \
             different"
        );
    }
    if settled_same + reordered + differing > 0 {
        out!(
            "order-dependent shaders' outputs: {settled_same} identical to the game's, {reordered} the same records in \
             another order, {differing} different"
        );
    }
    // What keeps an identical replay from proving the frame: what the capture could not record, used resources
    // without contents, and events replay could not run as recorded. What order-dependent events wrote is the game's
    // from there on; replay's own output was compared, but no exact comparison of it can hold.
    if differing > 0 {
        out!(
            "not compared: {differing} outputs of order-dependent draws and dispatches that differ from the game's in \
             more than order (the game's were used)"
        );
    }
    for note in c.rows(
        &format!("SELECT what, coalesce(detail, ''), count FROM gaps WHERE what IN ({CHECKS}) ORDER BY what, detail"),
        [],
        |r| {
            Ok(format!(
                "{} {} ({}x)",
                r.get::<_, String>(0)?,
                r.get::<_, String>(1)?,
                r.get::<_, i64>(2)?
            ))
        },
    ) {
        out!("not compared: {note}");
    }
    let mut incomplete: Vec<String> = c.rows(
        &format!("SELECT what, coalesce(detail, ''), count FROM gaps WHERE what NOT IN ({CHECKS}) ORDER BY what, detail"),
        [],
        |r| {
            Ok(format!(
                "capture gap: {} {} ({}x)",
                r.get::<_, String>(0)?,
                r.get::<_, String>(1)?,
                r.get::<_, i64>(2)?
            ))
        },
    );
    let missing: i64 = c
        .row(
            "SELECT count(*) FROM resources WHERE used = 1 AND content IS NULL",
            [],
            |r| r.get(0),
        )
        .unwrap_or(0);
    if missing > 0 {
        incomplete.push(format!("{missing} resources the frame used have no contents"));
    }
    incomplete.extend(b.warnings().into_iter().map(|w| format!("replay: {w}")));
    for i in &incomplete {
        out!("incomplete: {i}");
    }
    if limit.is_some_and(|l| compared >= l) {
        out!("(stopped after {compared} comparisons: --limit)");
    }
    let mut failed = Vec::new();
    if same < compared {
        failed.push(format!("{} of {compared} targets differ", compared - same));
    }
    if outputs_differing > 0 {
        failed.push(format!(
            "{outputs_differing} of {} outputs of draws and dispatches differ",
            outputs_same + outputs_differing
        ));
    }
    if !failed.is_empty() {
        return Err(failed.join("; "));
    }
    if compared == 0 {
        return Err("no target was compared".into());
    }
    if !incomplete.is_empty() {
        return Err(format!(
            "every target identical, but the capture is incomplete ({} reasons above)",
            incomplete.len()
        ));
    }
    Ok(())
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::same_records;

    #[test]
    fn records_in_another_order_are_the_same_records() {
        let a = [1u8, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8];
        let b = [5u8, 6, 7, 8, 1, 2, 3, 4];
        assert!(same_records(&a, &b, 4));
        // The same bytes, but not the same 4-byte records.
        let c = [1u8, 2, 7, 8, 5, 6, 3, 4];
        assert!(!same_records(&a, &c, 4));
        // As often each: a record twice is not the same as two records.
        assert!(!same_records(&[1, 1, 2, 2], &[1, 1, 1, 1], 2));
    }
}

```

`cli/src/resources.rs`:

```rs
//! `resources`, `resource`, `events` and `stack`: what was alive, what the frame did to it, and where from.

use locum_capture::format;
use rusqlite::types::Value;

use crate::describe::{self, SHAPE_COLUMNS, Shape, mib, shape, short};
use crate::open::Capture;
use crate::out;

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Filter {
    pub used: bool,
    pub written: bool,
    pub kind: Option<String>,
    pub format: Option<String>,
    pub hash: Option<String>,
    pub width: Option<i64>,
    pub height: Option<i64>,
}

pub fn resources(c: &Capture, f: &Filter) -> Result<(), String> {
    let mut wh: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut params: Vec<Value> = Vec::new();
    let mut param = |v: Value| {
        params.push(v);
        format!("?{}", params.len())
    };
    if f.used {
        wh.push("used = 1".into());
    }
    if f.written {
        wh.push("written = 1".into());
    }
    if let Some(k) = &f.kind {
        wh.push(format!("kind = {}", param(Value::Text(k.clone()))));
    }
    if let Some(name) = &f.format {
        let n = format::by_name(name).ok_or_else(|| format!("no DXGI format {name}"))?;
        wh.push(format!("format = {}", param(Value::Integer(i64::from(n)))));
    }
    if let Some(w) = f.width {
        wh.push(format!("width = {}", param(Value::Integer(w))));
    }
    if let Some(h) = f.height {
        wh.push(format!("height = {}", param(Value::Integer(h))));
    }
    if let Some(h) = &f.hash {
        let p = param(Value::Text(h.clone()));
        wh.push(format!(
            "(content LIKE {p} || '%' OR upload LIKE {p} || '%' OR id IN \
             (SELECT resource FROM subresources WHERE hash LIKE {p} || '%'))"
        ));
    }
    let sql = format!(
        "SELECT {SHAPE_COLUMNS}, used, written, content, content_source, upload, upload_stored, content_note \
         FROM resources {} ORDER BY id",
        if wh.is_empty() {
            String::new()
        } else {
            format!("WHERE {}", wh.join(" AND "))
        }
    );
    type Row = (
        Shape,
        bool,
        bool,
        Option<String>,
        Option<String>,
        Option<String>,
        bool,
        Option<String>,
    );
    let rows: Vec<Row> = c.rows(&sql, rusqlite::params_from_iter(params), |r| {
        Ok((
            Shape::from_row(r)?,
            r.get(12)?,
            r.get(13)?,
            r.get(14)?,
            r.get(15)?,
            r.get(16)?,
            r.get(17)?,
            r.get(18)?,
        ))
    });
    let mut total = 0u64;
    for (s, used, written, content, source, upload, stored, note) in &rows {
        total += s.bytes;
        let flags = format!(
            "{}{}",
            if *used { "U" } else { "-" },
            if *written { "W" } else { "-" }
        );
        let contents = match (content, source) {
            (Some(k), Some(src)) => format!("contents {} ({src})", short(k)),
            _ => String::new(),
        };
        let upload = upload
            .as_ref()
            .map(|u| format!("upload {}{}", short(u), if *stored { "" } else { " (hash)" }))
            .unwrap_or_default();
        out!(
            "{flags} {:<60} {contents:<32} {upload}{}",
            s.to_string(),
            note.as_ref().map(|n| format!("  [{n}]")).unwrap_or_default()
        );
    }
    out!(
        "{} resources, {}  (U used by the frame, W written by it)",
        rows.len(),
        mib(total)
    );
    Ok(())
}

pub fn resource(c: &Capture, id: i64) -> Result<(), String> {
    let s = shape(c, id).ok_or_else(|| format!("no resource #{id}"))?;
    type Row = (
        Option<i64>,
        Option<i64>,
        Option<i64>,
        Option<i64>,
        Option<i64>,
        Option<i64>,
        Option<i64>,
        Option<i64>,
        Option<String>,
        bool,
        Option<i64>,
        Option<i64>,
        i64,
        bool,
        bool,
        Option<String>,
        Option<String>,
        Option<String>,
    );
    let r: Row = c
        .row(
            "SELECT stride, usage, bind, cpu, misc, samples, created_frame, created_stack, upload, upload_stored, \
             updated_frame, updated_stack, update_count, used, written, content, content_source, content_note \
             FROM resources WHERE id = ?1",
            [id],
            |r| {
                Ok((
                    r.get(0)?,
                    r.get(1)?,
                    r.get(2)?,
                    r.get(3)?,
                    r.get(4)?,
                    r.get(5)?,
                    r.get(6)?,
                    r.get(7)?,
                    r.get(8)?,
                    r.get(9)?,
                    r.get(10)?,
                    r.get(11)?,
                    r.get(12)?,
                    r.get(13)?,
                    r.get(14)?,
                    r.get(15)?,
                    r.get(16)?,
                    r.get(17)?,
                ))
            },
        )
        .ok_or("no row")?;
    let (
        _stride,
        usage,
        bind,
        cpu,
        misc,
        _samples,
        created,
        created_stack,
        upload,
        stored,
        updated,
        updated_stack,
        updates,
        used,
        written,
        content,
        source,
        note,
    ) = r;
    out!("{s}  ({})", mib(s.bytes));
    out!(
        "usage {} bind 0x{:x} cpu 0x{:x} misc 0x{:x}",
        usage.unwrap_or(0),
        bind.unwrap_or(0),
        cpu.unwrap_or(0),
        misc.unwrap_or(0)
    );
    match created {
        Some(f) => out!("created at frame {f}"),
        None => out!("created before locum numbered it (frame unknown)"),
    }
    if let Some(st) = created_stack {
        print_stack(c, "  from", st, 8);
    }
    match (&upload, stored) {
        (Some(u), true) => out!("upload {u} (stored)"),
        (Some(u), false) => out!("upload {u} (hash only)"),
        _ => out!("no upload hash (created without data, or updated in parts)"),
    }
    if let Some(m) = c.names.of(c, id) {
        out!("made from {m}");
    }
    if updates > 0 {
        out!(
            "updated {updates} times, last at frame {}",
            updated.map_or("?".into(), |f| f.to_string())
        );
        if let Some(st) = updated_stack {
            print_stack(c, "  last from", st, 8);
        }
    }
    out!(
        "the frame {} it{}",
        if used { "used" } else { "did not use" },
        if written { " and wrote" } else { "" }
    );
    match (content, source) {
        (Some(k), Some(src)) => out!("contents as the frame began: {k} ({src})"),
        _ if used => out!("contents: missing"),
        _ => {}
    }
    if let Some(n) = note {
        out!("  note: {n}");
    }
    let subs: Vec<(i64, Option<String>)> = c.rows(
        "SELECT sub, hash FROM subresources WHERE resource = ?1 ORDER BY sub",
        [id],
        |r| Ok((r.get(0)?, r.get(1)?)),
    );
    if subs.len() > 1 {
        let layout = s.subs();
        out!("subresources:");
        for (sub, hash) in subs {
            let shape = layout.iter().find(|l| i64::from(l.index) == sub);
            out!(
                "  {sub:>4} {} {}",
                shape.map_or(String::new(), |l| format!(
                    "mip {} slice {} {}x{}{}",
                    l.mip,
                    l.slice,
                    l.width,
                    l.height,
                    if l.depth > 1 {
                        format!("x{}", l.depth)
                    } else {
                        String::new()
                    }
                )),
                hash.as_deref().unwrap_or("-")
            );
        }
    }
    let views: Vec<(i64, String, Option<String>)> = c.rows(
        "SELECT id, kind, json FROM views WHERE resource = ?1 ORDER BY id",
        [id],
        |r| Ok((r.get(0)?, r.get(1)?, r.get(2)?)),
    );
    for (v, kind, json) in views {
        out!("view #{v} {kind} {}", json.unwrap_or_default());
    }
    let bound: Vec<(i64, String, String, i64)> = c.rows(
        "SELECT draw, stage, kind, slot FROM bindings WHERE resource = ?1 ORDER BY draw",
        [id],
        |r| Ok((r.get(0)?, r.get(1)?, r.get(2)?, r.get(3)?)),
    );
    if !bound.is_empty() {
        out!("bound to {} draws:", bound.len());
        for (d, stage, kind, slot) in bound.iter().take(24) {
            out!("  draw {d}: {stage} {kind}{slot}");
        }
        if bound.len() > 24 {
            out!("  ... ({} more; `draws --uses {id}`)", bound.len() - 24);
        }
    }
    let events: Vec<(i64, String, String, String)> = c.rows(
        "SELECT e.seq, e.kind, e.call, x.access FROM event_resources x JOIN events e ON e.seq = x.event \
         WHERE x.resource = ?1 AND (x.access = 'write' OR e.kind NOT IN ('draw', 'dispatch')) ORDER BY e.seq",
        [id],
        |r| Ok((r.get(0)?, r.get(1)?, r.get(2)?, r.get(3)?)),
    );
    if !events.is_empty() {
        out!("events that wrote it or copied from it:");
        for (seq, kind, call, access) in events.iter().take(40) {
            out!("  event {seq}: {kind} {call} ({access})");
        }
        if events.len() > 40 {
            out!("  ... ({} more; `events --resource {id}`)", events.len() - 40);
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn print_stack(c: &Capture, label: &str, id: i64, depth: usize) {
    let frames = describe::stack(c, id);
    out!(
        "{label} stack {id}: {}",
        frames.iter().take(depth).cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" < ")
    );
}

pub struct EventFilter {
    pub kind: Option<String>,
    pub resource: Option<i64>,
    pub from: i64,
    pub limit: i64,
}

pub fn events(c: &Capture, f: &EventFilter) -> Result<(), String> {
    let mut wh = vec!["e.seq >= ?1".to_string()];
    let mut params: Vec<Value> = vec![Value::Integer(f.from)];
    if let Some(k) = &f.kind {
        params.push(Value::Text(k.clone()));
        wh.push(format!("e.kind = ?{}", params.len()));
    }
    if let Some(r) = f.resource {
        params.push(Value::Integer(r));
        wh.push(format!(
            "e.seq IN (SELECT event FROM event_resources WHERE resource = ?{})",
            params.len()
        ));
    }
    params.push(Value::Integer(f.limit));
    let sql = format!(
        "SELECT e.seq, e.kind, e.call, e.deferred, e.list, e.draw, e.args, e.data, \
         (SELECT group_concat(resource) FROM event_resources WHERE event = e.seq AND access = 'write') \
         FROM events e WHERE {} ORDER BY e.seq LIMIT ?{}",
        wh.join(" AND "),
        params.len()
    );
    type Row = (
        i64,
        String,
        String,
        bool,
        Option<i64>,
        Option<i64>,
        Option<String>,
        Option<String>,
        Option<String>,
    );
    let rows: Vec<Row> = c.rows(&sql, rusqlite::params_from_iter(params), |r| {
        Ok((
            r.get(0)?,
            r.get(1)?,
            r.get(2)?,
            r.get(3)?,
            r.get(4)?,
            r.get(5)?,
            r.get(6)?,
            r.get(7)?,
            r.get(8)?,
        ))
    });
    for (seq, kind, call, deferred, list, draw, args, data, writes) in rows {
        let place = if deferred {
            format!("list {}", list.map_or("?".into(), |l| l.to_string()))
        } else {
            "imm".into()
        };
        out!(
            "{seq:>6} {kind:<9} {call:<28} {place:<8} {}{}{}{}",
            draw.map(|d| format!("draw {d} ")).unwrap_or_default(),
            args.unwrap_or_default(),
            writes
                .map(|w| format!("  writes #{}", w.replace(',', " #")))
                .unwrap_or_default(),
            data.map(|d| format!("  data {}", short(&d))).unwrap_or_default()
        );
    }
    Ok(())
}

pub fn stack(c: &Capture, id: i64) -> Result<(), String> {
    let frames = describe::stack(c, id);
    if frames.is_empty() {
        return Err(format!("no stack {id}"));
    }
    for f in frames {
        out!("{f}");
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

`cli/src/shaders.rs`:

```rs
//! `shaders` and `shader`: the shaders the frame used, their constant buffers and disassembly.

use std::collections::HashMap;

use locum_capture::rdef;
use windows::Win32::Graphics::Direct3D::Fxc::D3DDisassemble;

use crate::open::Capture;
use crate::out;

pub fn shaders(c: &Capture) -> Result<(), String> {
    let mut uses: HashMap<String, i64> = HashMap::new();
    for stage in ["vs", "hs", "ds", "gs", "ps", "cs"] {
        let counts: Vec<(String, i64)> = c.rows(
            &format!("SELECT {stage}, count(*) FROM draws WHERE {stage} IS NOT NULL GROUP BY {stage}"),
            [],
            |r| Ok((r.get(0)?, r.get(1)?)),
        );
        for (h, n) in counts {
            *uses.entry(h).or_default() += n;
        }
    }
    let rows: Vec<(String, String, Option<i64>)> = c.rows(
        "SELECT hash, stage, size FROM shaders ORDER BY stage, hash",
        [],
        |r| Ok((r.get(0)?, r.get(1)?, r.get(2)?)),
    );
    out!("{:<5} {:<16} {:>7} {:>6}", "stage", "hash", "bytes", "draws");
    for (h, stage, size) in rows {
        out!(
            "{stage:<5} {h:<16} {:>7} {:>6}",
            size.map_or("-".into(), |s| s.to_string()),
            uses.get(&h).copied().unwrap_or(0)
        );
    }
    Ok(())
}

pub fn shader(c: &Capture, hash: &str, disassemble: bool) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (h, stage, key): (String, String, Option<String>) = c
        .row(
            "SELECT hash, stage, blob FROM shaders WHERE hash LIKE ?1 || '%' ORDER BY hash LIMIT 1",
            [hash],
            |r| Ok((r.get(0)?, r.get(1)?, r.get(2)?)),
        )
        .ok_or_else(|| format!("no shader {hash}"))?;
    let key = key.ok_or("its bytecode was not found when the capture was written")?;
    let code = c.blob(&key)?;
    out!("{stage} {h}: {} bytes, blob {key}", code.len());
    match rdef::constant_buffers(&code) {
        Some(cbs) => {
            for cb in cbs {
                out!(
                    "cbuffer {} : b{}{} ({} bytes)",
                    cb.name,
                    cb.slot.map_or("?".into(), |s| s.to_string()),
                    if cb.space != 0 {
                        format!(" space {}", cb.space)
                    } else {
                        String::new()
                    },
                    cb.size
                );
                for v in &cb.variables {
                    out!(
                        "  c{:<3} +{:<3} {:<4} {}{}",
                        v.offset / 16,
                        v.offset % 16,
                        v.size,
                        v.name,
                        if v.used { "" } else { "  (unused)" }
                    );
                }
            }
        }
        None => out!("no reflection (RDEF) in its bytecode"),
    }
    if disassemble {
        out!("");
        out!("{}", disassembly(&code)?);
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// The bytecode's disassembly, from the system's shader compiler.
pub fn disassembly(code: &[u8]) -> Result<String, String> {
    let blob = unsafe { D3DDisassemble(code.as_ptr().cast(), code.len(), 0, None) }
        .map_err(|e| format!("D3DDisassemble: {e}"))?;
    let text =
        unsafe { core::slice::from_raw_parts(blob.GetBufferPointer() as *const u8, blob.GetBufferSize()) };
    Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(text).trim_end_matches('\0').to_string())
}
```

```rs
//! locum's own copies on a game's context (contents, constants, targets) must run whatever predicate the game set:
//! copies and resolves are predicated, and one skipped by the game's predicate would leave a capture's copy empty.

use windows::Win32::Graphics::Direct3D11::*;
use windows::core::BOOL;

/// Runs `f` with predication off on `c`, then sets the game's predicate back.
///
/// # Safety
/// `c` must be a live context that nothing else uses meanwhile.
pub unsafe fn unpredicated<R>(c: &ID3D11DeviceContext, f: impl FnOnce() -> R) -> R {
    let mut predicate = None;
    let mut value = BOOL(0);
    unsafe { c.GetPredication(Some(&mut predicate), Some(&mut value)) };
    let Some(predicate) = predicate else {
        return f();
    };
    unsafe { c.SetPredication(None, false) };
    let r = f();
    unsafe { c.SetPredication(&predicate, value.as_bool()) };
    r
}
```

`d3d11/src/readback.rs`:

```rs
//! Reading a resource back: a GPU copy into a staging resource on some context, mapped later on the immediate context
//! and packed into the canonical layout (`locum_capture::layout`). Multisampled colour textures are resolved first;
//! depth textures are copied through their typeless format.

use locum_capture::format;
use locum_capture::layout::{self, Sub};
use windows::Win32::Graphics::Direct3D11::*;
use windows::Win32::Graphics::Dxgi::Common::*;
use windows::core::Interface;

/// A copy of a resource waiting to be read.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct Readback {
    staging: ID3D11Resource,
    pub subs: Vec<Sub>,
    buffer: bool,
}

impl Readback {
    /// Which copy this is: the same for every clone of it (a copy recorded in a command list is one copy however
    /// often the list runs).
    pub fn copy_id(&self) -> usize {
        self.staging.as_raw() as usize
    }
}

/// The typeless format a depth format's texture can be copied through.
fn copyable(f: u32) -> u32 {
    match f {
        20 => 19,
        40 => 39,
        45 => 44,
        55 => 53,
        other => other,
    }
}

/// A resource's subresources in the canonical layout, from its description.
pub fn subs(resource: &ID3D11Resource) -> Result<Vec<Sub>, String> {
    let no_layout = |f: DXGI_FORMAT| format!("format {} has no readable layout", format::name(f.0 as u32));
    unsafe {
        if let Ok(b) = resource.cast::<ID3D11Buffer>() {
            let mut d = D3D11_BUFFER_DESC::default();
            b.GetDesc(&mut d);
            return Ok(layout::buffer(d.ByteWidth));
        }
        if let Ok(t) = resource.cast::<ID3D11Texture2D>() {
            let mut d = D3D11_TEXTURE2D_DESC::default();
            t.GetDesc(&mut d);
            return layout::texture(d.Format.0 as u32, d.Width, d.Height, 1, d.MipLevels, d.ArraySize)
                .ok_or_else(|| no_layout(d.Format));
        }
        if let Ok(t) = resource.cast::<ID3D11Texture3D>() {
            let mut d = D3D11_TEXTURE3D_DESC::default();
            t.GetDesc(&mut d);
            return layout::texture(d.Format.0 as u32, d.Width, d.Height, d.Depth, d.MipLevels, 1)
                .ok_or_else(|| no_layout(d.Format));
        }
        if let Ok(t) = resource.cast::<ID3D11Texture1D>() {
            let mut d = D3D11_TEXTURE1D_DESC::default();
            t.GetDesc(&mut d);
            return layout::texture(d.Format.0 as u32, d.Width, 1, 1, d.MipLevels, d.ArraySize)
                .ok_or_else(|| no_layout(d.Format));
        }
    }
    Err("not a buffer or texture".into())
}

/// The bytes a readback of `resource` holds: its subresources in the canonical layout.
pub fn bytes(resource: &ID3D11Resource) -> Result<u64, String> {
    Ok(subs(resource)?.iter().map(|s| s.size).sum())
}

/// Records a copy of `resource` into a new staging resource on `c`, whatever predicate `c` has set.
///
/// # Safety
/// `c` must be a context of the device that made `resource`.
pub unsafe fn issue(c: &ID3D11DeviceContext, resource: &ID3D11Resource) -> Result<Readback, String> {
    unsafe { crate::predication::unpredicated(c, || issue_now(c, resource)) }
}

unsafe fn issue_now(c: &ID3D11DeviceContext, resource: &ID3D11Resource) -> Result<Readback, String> {
    let device = unsafe { c.GetDevice() }.map_err(|e| format!("no device: {e}"))?;
    let subs = subs(resource)?;
    if let Ok(b) = resource.cast::<ID3D11Buffer>() {
        let mut d = D3D11_BUFFER_DESC::default();
        unsafe { b.GetDesc(&mut d) };
        let sd = D3D11_BUFFER_DESC {
            ByteWidth: d.ByteWidth,
            Usage: D3D11_USAGE_STAGING,
            CPUAccessFlags: D3D11_CPU_ACCESS_READ.0 as u32,
            ..Default::default()
        };
        let mut s = None;
        unsafe { device.CreateBuffer(&sd, None, Some(&mut s)) }
            .map_err(|e| format!("staging buffer: {e}"))?;
        let s = s.ok_or("no staging buffer")?;
        unsafe { c.CopyResource(&s, resource) };
        return Ok(Readback {
            staging: s.cast().expect("a buffer is a resource"),
            subs,
            buffer: true,
        });
    }
    let staging: ID3D11Resource = if let Ok(t) = resource.cast::<ID3D11Texture2D>() {
        let mut d = D3D11_TEXTURE2D_DESC::default();
        unsafe { t.GetDesc(&mut d) };
        let mut source: ID3D11Resource = resource.clone();
        if d.SampleDesc.Count > 1 {
            if format::is_depth(d.Format.0 as u32) {
                return Err("multisampled depth cannot be resolved".into());
            }
            let typed = DXGI_FORMAT(format::readable(d.Format.0 as u32) as i32);
            let resolved = D3D11_TEXTURE2D_DESC {
                MipLevels: 1,
                Format: typed,
                SampleDesc: DXGI_SAMPLE_DESC { Count: 1, Quality: 0 },
                Usage: D3D11_USAGE_DEFAULT,
                BindFlags: 0,
                CPUAccessFlags: 0,
                MiscFlags: 0,
                ..d
            };
            let mut r = None;
            unsafe { device.CreateTexture2D(&resolved, None, Some(&mut r)) }
                .map_err(|e| format!("texture to resolve into: {e}"))?;
            let r = r.ok_or("no texture to resolve into")?;
            for slice in 0..d.ArraySize {
                unsafe { c.ResolveSubresource(&r, slice, resource, slice, typed) };
            }
            source = r.cast().expect("a texture is a resource");
            d = resolved;
        }
        let sd = D3D11_TEXTURE2D_DESC {
            Format: DXGI_FORMAT(copyable(d.Format.0 as u32) as i32),
            Usage: D3D11_USAGE_STAGING,
            BindFlags: 0,
            CPUAccessFlags: D3D11_CPU_ACCESS_READ.0 as u32,
            MiscFlags: 0,
            ..d
        };
        let mut s = None;
        unsafe { device.CreateTexture2D(&sd, None, Some(&mut s)) }.map_err(|e| {
            format!(
                "staging texture of format {}: {e}",
                format::name(sd.Format.0 as u32)
            )
        })?;
        let s = s.ok_or("no staging texture")?;
        unsafe { c.CopyResource(&s, &source) };
        s.cast().expect("a texture is a resource")
    } else if let Ok(t) = resource.cast::<ID3D11Texture3D>() {
        let mut d = D3D11_TEXTURE3D_DESC::default();
        unsafe { t.GetDesc(&mut d) };
        let sd = D3D11_TEXTURE3D_DESC {
            Usage: D3D11_USAGE_STAGING,
            BindFlags: 0,
            CPUAccessFlags: D3D11_CPU_ACCESS_READ.0 as u32,
            MiscFlags: 0,
            ..d
        };
        let mut s = None;
        unsafe { device.CreateTexture3D(&sd, None, Some(&mut s)) }
            .map_err(|e| format!("staging volume: {e}"))?;
        let s = s.ok_or("no staging volume")?;
        unsafe { c.CopyResource(&s, resource) };
        s.cast().expect("a texture is a resource")
    } else if let Ok(t) = resource.cast::<ID3D11Texture1D>() {
        let mut d = D3D11_TEXTURE1D_DESC::default();
        unsafe { t.GetDesc(&mut d) };
        let sd = D3D11_TEXTURE1D_DESC {
            Format: DXGI_FORMAT(copyable(d.Format.0 as u32) as i32),
            Usage: D3D11_USAGE_STAGING,
            BindFlags: 0,
            CPUAccessFlags: D3D11_CPU_ACCESS_READ.0 as u32,
            MiscFlags: 0,
            ..d
        };
        let mut s = None;
        unsafe { device.CreateTexture1D(&sd, None, Some(&mut s)) }.map_err(|e| format!("staging 1D: {e}"))?;
        let s = s.ok_or("no staging 1D texture")?;
        unsafe { c.CopyResource(&s, resource) };
        s.cast().expect("a texture is a resource")
    } else {
        return Err("not a buffer or texture".into());
    };
    Ok(Readback {
        staging,
        subs,
        buffer: false,
    })
}

impl Readback {
    /// The bytes it holds in the canonical layout. Waits for the GPU.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    /// `immediate` must be the immediate context of the device that made the copy.
    pub unsafe fn read(&self, immediate: &ID3D11DeviceContext) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
        let mut bytes = Vec::with_capacity(layout::total(&self.subs) as usize);
        for sub in &self.subs {
            let mut mapped = D3D11_MAPPED_SUBRESOURCE::default();
            unsafe { immediate.Map(&self.staging, sub.index, D3D11_MAP_READ, 0, Some(&mut mapped)) }
                .map_err(|e| format!("map of subresource {}: {e}", sub.index))?;
            let (row, slice) = if self.buffer {
                (sub.row_bytes as usize, sub.slice_bytes() as usize)
            } else {
                (mapped.RowPitch as usize, mapped.DepthPitch as usize)
            };
            unsafe { layout::pack(sub, mapped.pData.cast(), row, slice, &mut bytes) };
            unsafe { immediate.Unmap(&self.staging, sub.index) };
        }
        Ok(bytes)
    }
}

```

`docs/README.md`:

```md
# locum reference

How locum works, the files it writes and reads, what a capture holds, and every `locum-cli` command. The
[README](../README.md) has the short version.

## How it works

- `d3d11.dll` and `dxgi.dll` contain no code: each export forwards to `locum.dll` (the same names and ordinals as the
  system DLLs, the list DXVK exports).
- `locum.dll` loads its own two DLLs, then the real `d3d11.dll` and `dxgi.dll` from the system folder, and wraps the
  device, its contexts, the DXGI factory and the swap chains in objects of its own. Loading its own first keeps a
  game that loads `d3d11.dll` late, by name, on locum's.
- The wrappers are generated. The `windows` crate publishes each interface's vtable as a `#[repr(C)]` struct with the
  exact ABI; `cargo xtask gen` reads those structs and writes `locum/src/vtables/`: one forwarding thunk per method
  and a trait whose default methods call the real object. A wrapper overrides only the methods it cares about.

## Files and settings

locum writes to the folder named by `LOCUM_DIR`, or `%LOCALAPPDATA%\locum`:

- `locum.log`: what was wrapped, the frame rate every 600 frames, and each interface the game asked for that locum
  passes to the real object unwrapped.
- `shaders/<hash>.<stage>.dxbc`: the bytecode of every shader the game creates, once per distinct shader. The hash
  is FNV-1a 64 of the bytecode.
- `captures/<name>/capture.db`: a captured frame (below). Create a file named `capture` in the folder to request one;
  locum removes it, records the next frames and writes the capture. Each line of the file is an option, and an empty
  file captures everything:
  - `label NAME`: the capture's folder name (default `frame-<n>`);
  - `skip targets`: no render and depth targets read back at the end of each pass;
  - `skip contents`: no resource contents (draws, state and constants only);
  - `max_mb N`: the most memory the copies of targets and of what draws and dispatches wrote through UAVs may use
    (default 4096); copies past it are skipped and counted.
- `blobs/<2 hex>/<32 hex>`: the blob store, shared by every capture: resource contents, targets, the bytes each update
  and map wrote, and shader bytecode, each under the xxh3-128 hash of its bytes. Contents are in a canonical layout:
  subresources in order (mip within array slice), rows packed tightly, blocks for compressed formats.
- `settings.txt` (written by you), one per line:
  - `uploads store` (default), `hash` or `off`: whether the data each resource is created with, and each update
    covering a whole subresource, is hashed and stored as it happens. Stored uploads are the game's own textures and
    meshes without a readback, and their hashes match the files they were loaded from when those hold the same bytes;
  - `blobs DIR`: where the blob store is (the variable `LOCUM_BLOBS` overrides it);
  - `dumper PATH`: `locum-cli.exe`, which writes a memory dump of the game at each capture (unless the request says
    `skip memory`). The game waits in Present only while it takes a snapshot of the process (tens of milliseconds);
    the dump is written from the snapshot while the game runs on;
  - `dumps DIR`: where the dumps go (default the capture's folder). They hold all of the game's memory: keep them
    private.
- `overrides.txt` (written by you): rules that change what is drawn, read again when the file changes and dropped when
  it is removed. One per line:
  - `skip vs=<hash>`: draws with that shader bound are not drawn (`skip cs=<hash>`: dispatches are not run);
  - `solid vs=<hash> R G B A`: those draws get a pixel shader writing that colour to every target;
  - `shader ps=<hash> FILE`: that shader is replaced by the bytecode in FILE (relative to the folder);
  - `constant ps b3 c0 X Y Z W`: the draw sees constant 0 of its ps b3 range as X Y Z W (floats, or `0x` and 8 hex
    digits for raw bits);
  - any rule can end with `if vs=<hash> ps=<hash> ...`; every stage can be named (vs hs ds gs ps cs).

  Hashes are the whole 16 hex digits here. Rules given to `locum-cli replay` can use the start of a hash instead,
  as long as it names exactly one shader of that stage in the capture.

  Rules apply at the draw, on its own context, and are undone after it. A changed constant is written into a GPU copy
  of the bound buffer, so draws on deferred contexts get theirs when their command list runs. `locum.log` reports how
  often each rule applied every 600 frames.

locum numbers every resource as it is created and keeps its description, creation stack and upload hash, so a
capture lists all the resources alive, not only those the frame touched. The capture runs over two frames: the one
before records command lists ahead of time (a list recorded then may be executed in the captured frame), and during
the captured frame every call is recorded.

Each resource's contents as the frame began are copied on the immediate context just before the first thing on the
GPU's timeline that touches it: before an immediate-context call that reads or writes it, or before the
`ExecuteCommandList` whose list touches it first. Nothing has touched it since the frame began, so the copy is exact
whatever the frame does to it later, on whichever context, and however many times a list runs; a list recorded but
never executed changes nothing. Immutable resources whose upload was stored are not copied: the upload is their
contents. locum's own copies run whatever predicate the game has set.

`capture.db` has these tables (`capture/src/db.rs` has the schema with comments):

- `meta`: the API, frame, process, request and counts; `gaps`: what could not be recorded, and why;
- `resources` and `subresources`: every live resource with its description, upload hash, whether the frame used or
  wrote it, and the key of its contents as the frame began with where they came from (`first-use` or `upload`) and
  any doubt about them;
- `views` and `states` (rasterizer, blend, depth-stencil, sampler, input layout), with their descriptions;
- `events`: everything on the GPU's timeline in order: draws, dispatches, clears, copies, updates and maps (with the
  key of the bytes written), resolves and mip generation, each with its context, command list and call stack;
- `draws`, `bindings`, `viewports`, `scissors`: each draw's shaders and state, and everything bound to it by stage,
  kind (`cb`, `srv`, `uav`, `sampler`, `rtv`, `dsv`, `vb`, `ib`, `so`) and slot, constant buffers with the bytes the
  GPU read (`cb_data`);
- `passes` and `targets`: runs of draws with the same targets, and the targets read back after each one's last draw
  (in the format the pass drew in; depth as the colour format of the same bits, D24S8 as R24_UNORM_X8);
- `results`: what each draw or dispatch wrote through its UAVs, as the GPU wrote it, and whether its shader is
  order-dependent (below);
- `shaders`, `modules`, `stacks`: bytecode keys, and what the call stacks need to be read.

Some shaders write different bytes depending on the order the GPU happens to run their threads: a thread that takes
the next free slot of a buffer with an atomic add (particles, light lists) puts its record wherever it lands, and the
GPU never runs the threads in the same order twice. locum reads every shader's bytecode as it is made and flags those
that use an atomic that returns a value (`imm_atomic_*`, `atomic_cmp_store`; `locum_capture::dxbc`), and the log
names them. During a capture, every draw or dispatch has everything bound to it as a UAV copied right after it runs,
into `results`, flagged when its shader is order-dependent.

While a capture is recording, the game's writes through `Map` go to memory locum owns and are copied to the driver's
at `Unmap`, so a map records only the bytes the game wrote. A discarding map starts as a fixed pattern
(`locum_capture::maps`), which is what the GPU reads wherever the game wrote nothing; replay writes the same pattern
under the recorded bytes, so a shader reading past what the game filled in sees what it saw in the game. Any other map
starts as the resource's memory and gets back only the words the game changed, so what the game left alone stays as
it was (a staging resource the GPU copied into keeps that copy). A swap chain resize during a capture gives the
capture up (it holds references to the back buffers): request another.

A pass ends where the targets in effect change on the GPU's timeline: an `OMSetRenderTargets` that binds other
targets, a command list whose first draw uses other targets than the draw before it, or the end of the frame. Its
targets are read there, and the capture records the event they were read after (the pass's last draw, or a clear, copy
or dispatch after it), which is where verify compares them. A command list executed more than once makes its copies
into the same places each time, so only its last execution's constants and targets are kept.

Draws recorded on deferred contexts are placed where their command list is executed. Constant buffers and targets
are copied by the GPU on the draw's own context, so each draw's constants and each pass's targets are the ones the
GPU saw at that point of the frame.

## Reading a capture

`locum-cli` reads captures. A capture is named by its `capture.db`, its folder, its name under locum's folder, or
`last`:

```
locum-cli captures                         # the captures in locum's folder, newest first
locum-cli info last                        # what it holds, and what it is missing
locum-cli draws last --ps 9f2c --pass 3    # draws, filtered by shader, pass, --uses/--target RESOURCE, --content KEY
locum-cli draw last 120                    # one draw: state, everything bound, constants by name, targets after it
locum-cli cb last 120 ps 3                 # a constant buffer, every register, named from the shader's reflection
locum-cli find last 0.35                   # which constant holds 0.35, its name, and the draws that saw it
locum-cli passes last
locum-cli resources last --used --format BC7_UNORM
locum-cli resource last 812                # where it was made (call stack), hashes, views, draws, events
locum-cli events last --kind copy          # the timeline; --resource N for what touched one resource
locum-cli shader last 9f2c -d              # constant buffers and disassembly
locum-cli export last 812 -o tex.dds       # contents as the frame began: .dds (all of it), .png (one mip), or raw
locum-cli target last 120 rt0 -o gbuf0.png # a target read back after a pass
locum-cli sql last "SELECT ..."            # anything else
```

Replay runs a captured draw again offline, on the GPU or on WARP (`--warp`), with or without rules in the
`overrides.txt` language changing it:

```
locum-cli verify last                      # replay the frame; compare every target read back with the game's
locum-cli replay last 812                  # the draw and the earlier events it depends on; writes its targets
locum-cli replay last last --rule "constant vs b11 c0 8 8 0 0"   # before, after and a diff picture of the change
locum-cli replay last 812 --rules mine.txt --mode frame
```

`verify` exits with success only when every target and every output of a draw or dispatch compared is identical and
nothing the replay needs is missing (contents, command lists, constants); checks the capture could not make (targets
or outputs skipped, a repeated list's earlier executions, the memory dump) are listed as not compared.

After each draw or dispatch, replay compares what it wrote through UAVs with what the game's GPU wrote (`results`).
Where it differs, `verify` names the event (`Dispatch 218 (event 567) #4770: wrote other bytes than the game's`),
fails, and goes on from the game's bytes, so a difference further on is that later event's own: the first such line
is where the replay and the game part. `replay` with rules puts back only order-dependent outputs, so a rule's
effect on a dispatch stays.

An order-dependent draw or dispatch's output is compared the same way, and described: identical; the same records in
another order (a structured buffer's structures, otherwise 4-byte words); or different in more than order, as when
the shader writes what its atomics returned (Sekiro's light tiles each hold the offset into the light list their
group was given). Then it puts the game's bytes in place and goes on from them, so everything after follows the
game's order and can be compared exactly. Neither is a failure. Outputs that differ in
more than order are listed as not compared: what verify proves is that every target is the game's given what those
events wrote in the game. Rules do not change what such an event writes.

A draw is replayed with what it depends on: walking back from it, each earlier event that wrote a resource it (or an
event already taken) reads or writes is taken too, and every resource starts with its contents as the frame began.
Each draw runs from the full state captured at it, with its constant buffers made from the bytes the GPU read. With
rules, the targets are written before (`rt0.before.png`) and after (`rt0.after.png`) them, and `rt0.diff.png` shows
the texels that changed in magenta over the unchanged ones in grey.

The memory dump ties what the GPU saw back to the game's memory:

```
locum-cli memfind last --cb 812 ps 3       # where each register of that constant buffer sits in memory
locum-cli memfind last --float 0.35        # or --int N, --bytes 0000803f
locum-cli memdiff before.dmp after.dmp --from 0.35 --to 0.5   # what changed between two dumps
locum-cli stack last 17                    # a call stack recorded at a map or update, as module+offset
```

Each hit is named: a module and offset, a thread's stack, or a heap allocation and the offset into it. Material
parameters copied straight into constant buffers are found this way; values the game computes each frame (matrices)
usually are not in memory as the GPU saw them.

Two captures, of the same game run twice or of a scene before and after a change, are compared draw by draw:

```
locum-cli diff before after                # how many draws match, and what differs in how many of them
locum-cli diff before after --draws        # each matched draw that differs, line by line
```

Draws are matched by what stays the same across a relaunch: their shaders, the call and its counts, the upload hashes
of the textures and buffers they read (or their shapes, for what the frame wrote), the shapes of their targets, and
how many draws like them came before. Matched draws are compared constant by constant (named from the shaders),
input by input and state by state.

A capture's textures and buffers are named from the files they were made from with an index of those files, keyed
the way captures key contents (a texture's canonical layout is a DDS file's order, so a DDS file is keyed whole and
mip by mip as it is):

```
locum-cli index files.db DIR...            # key every DDS file under each DIR
locum-cli --index files.db join last       # what each texture and buffer the frame used was made from
locum-cli --index files.db draw last 120   # bound resources are shown with their file's name
```

A resource is matched by its upload, its contents, or subresource by subresource (a texture made from fewer mips
than its file holds, or from one face). `LOCUM_INDEX` (paths separated by `;`) stands in for `--index`. A game's own
extractor can add what it reads from its archives through `locum_capture::index`.

Constants are named from each shader's reflection, as `cbuffer.variable[index].component`. PNGs of depth and other
one-channel images are stretched from their smallest to largest value, float colour is tone-mapped, and `--range
LO:HI` sets the mapping.

## References

DXVK and RenderDoc are both open source and solve the same problems (object identity, DXGI, deferred contexts); when
in doubt, locum does what they do.
```

`locum/src/com.rs`:
